paper.title: MA-VLA: Multi-Arm Vision-Language-Action Model for Collaboration and Compositional Generalization
paper.summary: Multi-arm collaboration is becoming a core capability in embodied manipulation. Recent vision-language-action (VLA) models integrate perception, language, and control, but most represent language as a single global instruction and do not provide an explicit mechanism for assigning and composing arm-specific behaviors. This design limits transfer to collaboration patterns that differ from those observed during training. We present MA-VLA, a unified framework for multi-arm collaboration via atomic action assignment. MA-VLA decomposes cooperative behavior into mid-level atomic prompts and allocates them to individual arms, enabling explicit subgoal specification and compositional reuse across tasks. To reduce reliance on fixed execution roles, we introduce Arm Shuffle, a training-time permutation of the observation, state, and assigned atomic prompts for each arm. This permutation enforces role-agnostic instruction following and supports recomposition into unseen coordination patterns, which we term multi-arm compositional generalization. We also construct a benchmark in which test-time collaboration patterns are absent in training set. Across simulation and real-world evaluations, prior state-of-the-art VLAs largely fail under these unseen collaborations, while MA-VLA consistently succeeds. These results indicate that structured, per-arm atomic action assignment offers a practical route to scalable generalization in multi-arm embodied systems. Code, models, and data are available at https://github.com/zhangzaibin/future-robots

analysis.problem_statement: Current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models lack an explicit mechanism for assigning and composing arm-specific behaviors, limiting their ability to generalize to unseen multi-arm collaboration patterns.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Compositional generalization and role-agnostic instruction following in multi-agent embodied systems.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the limitation of global instruction representation in multi-arm robotics by introducing a framework that decomposes cooperative behavior into atomic, arm-specific prompts. By enforcing role-agnosticism through training-time permutation, the model achieves compositional generalization to unseen coordination patterns, a critical step toward scalable and flexible robotic collaboration.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Success rate on unseen collaboration patterns
key_metrics.baseline: Prior state-of-the-art VLAs

technical_breakdown.method: The model decomposes cooperative tasks into mid-level atomic prompts allocated to individual arms, allowing for explicit subgoal specification and compositional reuse.
technical_breakdown.architecture: A unified VLA framework incorporating atomic action assignment and a mechanism for per-arm prompt allocation.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Utilizes 'Arm Shuffle,' a training-time permutation of observations, states, and assigned atomic prompts for each arm to enforce role-agnostic instruction following.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not specified in the provided metadata.

paper.title: DEFUSE: Generalizable Backdoor Defense for Self-Supervised Encoders with Generative Priors
paper.summary: Self-supervised learning (SSL) encoders are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, posing threats to both visual SSL encoders and vision-language encoders. Existing defenses are typically designed for only one of these paradigms and rely on restrictive assumptions such as access to uninfected in-distribution data or precomputed pseudo-labels, which are difficult to satisfy in practice. To address these limitations, we propose DEFUSE, a generalizable backdoor detection framework for SSL encoders. Inspired by Bayesian posterior inference, we reformulate backdoor detection as a representation-conditioned image likelihood estimation problem parameterized by a conditional diffusion generative model. Uninfected representations tend to yield semantically consistent reconstructions, whereas backdoored ones are more likely to be mapped to the attacker's target class or semantically meaningless images, deviating from the original semantics and thereby exposing the backdoor. However, we find that the exact likelihood is intractable, because highly abstracted representations discard the low-level information necessary for pixel-faithful reconstruction. We therefore relax the objective to semantic reconstruction and evaluate it in a well-separated representation space provided by a reference encoder. Rather than training from scratch, we fine-tune a pretrained diffusion model, leveraging its generative prior to map data onto the natural image manifold while preserving semantic content. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DEFUSE substantially outperforms existing detectors across diverse attack settings, generalizing to both visual SSL and vision-language encoders. Notably, our method greatly reduces the reliance on prior knowledge about the victim encoder or the attack strategy. The source code is available at https://github.com/jsrdcht/DEFUSE .

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the lack of generalizable backdoor defenses for self-supervised learning (SSL) encoders that do not rely on restrictive assumptions like access to clean in-distribution data or specific attack knowledge.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Security and robustness of self-supervised representation learning models against adversarial backdoor attacks.
analysis.executive_summary: This work is significant because it bridges the gap between visual SSL and vision-language encoder security, providing a unified defense mechanism that removes practical barriers such as the need for uninfected data or pseudo-labels. By leveraging generative priors, it offers a more realistic and deployable solution for securing foundation models in real-world scenarios where attack specifics are unknown.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Outperformance of existing backdoor detectors across diverse attack settings
key_metrics.baseline: Existing backdoor detection frameworks for SSL encoders

technical_breakdown.method: Reformulates backdoor detection as representation-conditioned image likelihood estimation using a conditional diffusion model, relaxing the objective to semantic reconstruction in a well-separated representation space.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Fine-tuned pretrained diffusion model, reference encoder for representation space, and SSL encoder under test.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses Bayesian posterior inference inspiration; maps data onto the natural image manifold while preserving semantic content; evaluates semantic consistency of reconstructions to identify backdoored representations.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Requires fine-tuning a diffusion model and inference via a reference encoder; computational cost depends on the diffusion sampling steps and encoder forward passes.

paper.title: D3ER: Supporting Multi-Modal Recommendation via Disentangle and Distillation-based Dynamic Ensemble
paper.summary: Incorporating items' information shared among multiple modalities into a fused representation, multi-modal recommendation (MR) has demonstrated documented success than canonical unimodal recommendation. Although several attempts have been made to extract the discriminative information unique in each modality, existing methods suffer from a core limitation: the joint learning of modal-homogeneity discriminative information (HOI) and modal-heterogeneity discriminative information (HEI) tends to weaken their individual effectiveness. To remedy this deficiency, we propose a novel method, dubbed Disentangle and Distillation-based Dynamic Ensemble for multi-modal Recommendation (D3ER). We introduce gradient boosting into MR for the first time to formalize the optimization objective for alternately learning HOI and HEI. This design enables models dedicated to each type of information to focus on their proficient samples, thereby promoting specialized optimization. Furthermore, to mitigate the inherent high storage cost and risk of local optima in gradient boosting, we enhance our framework with knowledge distillation and a global correction regularization. Experiments on prevalent real-world datasets confirm the superiority of our proposed method on MR.

analysis.problem_statement: The joint learning of modal-homogeneity and modal-heterogeneity discriminative information in multi-modal recommendation systems tends to weaken the individual effectiveness of each information type.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Information interference and suboptimal specialization in multi-modal feature fusion.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the degradation of performance in multi-modal recommendation caused by the conflict between learning shared and unique modal features. By introducing gradient boosting to alternate between learning these distinct information types, it enables specialized optimization for each modality aspect. This approach offers a novel structural solution to improve recommendation accuracy by mitigating the negative transfer often seen in joint multi-modal learning.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Superiority on Multi-Modal Recommendation tasks
key_metrics.baseline: Existing multi-modal recommendation methods

technical_breakdown.method: The method uses gradient boosting to formalize an optimization objective that alternates between learning modal-homogeneity discriminative information (HOI) and modal-heterogeneity discriminative information (HEI). This allows dedicated models to focus on their proficient samples. Knowledge distillation and global correction regularization are added to mitigate storage costs and local optima risks associated with gradient boosting.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Disentangle and Distillation-based Dynamic Ensemble (D3ER) framework.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Gradient boosting for alternating optimization, knowledge distillation, global correction regularization.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: High storage cost inherent to gradient boosting is mitigated by knowledge distillation; specific computational complexity figures are not provided in the abstract.

paper.title: Moving Beyond More Views: Redundancy-Aware Ego-Exo Fusion for Proficiency Estimation
paper.summary: EgoExo proficiency estimation aims to assess action quality by integrating fine-grained motion cues from egocentric (1st-person) views with spatial context from multiple exocentric (3rd-person) views. Simply adding more exocentric views degrades EgoExo performance, as redundant or noisy perspectives dilute useful motion cues. Our analysis identifies two key causes: (1) Multiview redundancy - From the data perspective, certain views provide limited or noisy information, diluting discriminative cues; (2) Overfitting - From the feature perspective, conventional fusion increases representational complexity, causing the model to memorise view-specific patterns rather than learn generalisable representations. To address these issues, we propose two complementary modules: AdaMVS, which adaptively identifies and fuses the most informative view tokens under weak supervision from the data perspective, and VIB-GB, which combines Gradient Blending and Variational Information Bottleneck regularisation from the feature perspective to compress redundant signals and suppress overfitting during training. Experiments on EgoExo-4D and EgoExo-Fitness demonstrate that our method learns both which view to look at and how to fuse them, achieving new state-of-the-art results. Our source code is available at https://github.com/dx199771/AdaMVS

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the degradation of Ego-Exo proficiency estimation performance caused by the introduction of redundant or noisy exocentric views that dilute discriminative motion cues and induce overfitting.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Multimodal fusion inefficiency and representational overfitting in multi-view video understanding.
analysis.executive_summary: This work challenges the assumption that adding more camera views improves action quality assessment, demonstrating that redundancy often harms performance. By introducing adaptive view selection and information bottleneck regularization, it enables models to learn robust, generalizable representations from heterogeneous ego-exo perspectives.

key_metrics.primary_metric: State-of-the-art proficiency estimation accuracy
key_metrics.baseline: Conventional Ego-Exo fusion methods

technical_breakdown.method: A dual-module approach combining data-driven adaptive view fusion with feature-level regularization to mitigate redundancy and overfitting.
technical_breakdown.architecture: AdaMVS (Adaptive Multi-View Selection) for token-level view fusion and VIB-GB (Variational Information Bottleneck with Gradient Blending) for feature compression.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: AdaMVS uses weak supervision to identify informative view tokens; VIB-GB applies Gradient Blending and Variational Information Bottleneck to compress redundant signals.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not specified in abstract

paper.title: InteractGesture: Progressive Chunk Guidance for Continuous Streaming Co-Speech Gesture Control
paper.summary: Co-speech gesture generation has made significant progress toward realistic full-body motion from speaker audio, yet existing models lack fine-grained spatial controllability of individual joints. To address this, we introduce \emph{InteractGesture}, a model-agnostic, inference-time method for spatially controllable gesture generation. \emph{InteractGesture} guides target latent estimates of a diffusion sampler through a differentiable RVQ-VAE decoder, backpropagating spatial control gradients to adjust motion latents during sampling. A primary challenge in streaming co-speech generation is chunk-wise dependency: standard sequential inference freezes prior chunks, preventing spatial constraints in future chunks from adjusting preceding trajectories and causing boundary inconsistencies. To overcome this limitation, we propose \emph{Progressive Chunk Guidance}, a chunk-window strategy that maintains an active set of editable chunk latents with staggered delays, enabling spatial constraints to propagate gradients backward across chunk boundaries during streaming generation. Experiments on the BEAT2 dataset show that \emph{InteractGesture} improves multi-joint spatial control while preserving overall gesture quality. Furthermore, our approach supports diverse applications, including sparse joint positioning, dense joint trajectory control, and directional pointing. Our project page is available at https://exitudio.github.io/interactgesture-page .

analysis.problem_statement: Existing co-speech gesture generation models lack fine-grained spatial controllability of individual joints and suffer from boundary inconsistencies in streaming inference due to frozen prior chunks.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Lack of fine-grained spatial control and temporal consistency in streaming generative models for human motion.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the critical limitation of current co-speech gesture systems that cannot precisely control specific joint positions or trajectories, which is essential for interactive social avatars. By introducing an inference-time guidance method that propagates spatial constraints backward across chunk boundaries, it enables real-time, fine-grained control without retraining the base model, significantly enhancing the utility of generative motion models for interactive applications.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Improvement in multi-joint spatial control while preserving gesture quality
key_metrics.baseline: Standard sequential inference / existing co-speech gesture models

technical_breakdown.method: Model-agnostic inference-time guidance using a differentiable RVQ-VAE decoder to backpropagate spatial control gradients to adjust motion latents during diffusion sampling.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Diffusion sampler, differentiable RVQ-VAE decoder, Progressive Chunk Guidance module with staggered delays.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Progressive Chunk Guidance maintains an active set of editable chunk latents to allow spatial constraints to propagate gradients backward across chunk boundaries, preventing the freezing of prior chunks in standard sequential inference.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Inference-time method (no training required for the control mechanism), but involves backpropagation through the decoder during sampling, increasing computational cost per inference step compared to standard sampling.

paper.title: CloSeR: Unified Relational Distillation from Closed-Set Teachers for Category Discovery
paper.summary: Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) is an intriguing open-world problem that has garnered increasing attention: given partially labelled data, the goal is to correctly recognize known classes while discovering coherent novel categories from unlabelled samples. Recent GCD methods typically adapt foundation models by jointly optimizing supervised classification and unsupervised discovery objectives on mixed labelled and unlabelled data. While effective, this coupled training can entangle closed-set recognition and open-set discovery, leading to objective conflict and biased predictions, and may disturb the semantic geometry of pretrained representations under limited labels and noisy pseudo-labels. We propose CloSeR, a simple plug-and-play framework that injects Closed-Set Relational knowledge into GCD training. CloSeR first builds a domain-adapted closed-set teacher by tuning lightweight block-wise adapters on labelled known-class data while keeping the foundation model backbone frozen, thereby preserving pretrained priors at low training cost. It then transfers the teacher's knowledge to downstream GCD via Unified Relational Distillation (URD), which distills complementary global sample-to-prototype relations to anchor known-class semantics and local sample-to-sample relations to preserve neighborhood structure, using separate feature pathways to reduce optimization interference. CloSeR is head-agnostic and readily integrates with both parametric and non-parametric GCD methods. Extensive experiments with DINO and DINOv2 backbones on six benchmarks (CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet-100, CUB, Stanford-Cars, and FGVC-Aircraft) show consistent gains over GCD baselines, achieving state-of-the-art performance. Project page: https://visual-ai.github.io/closer/
paper.comment: Accepted as a conference paper at ECCV 2026

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the objective conflict and semantic geometry distortion caused by jointly optimizing supervised classification and unsupervised discovery objectives in Generalized Category Discovery (GCD).
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Objective conflict and representation entanglement in open-world learning with limited labels.
analysis.executive_summary: CloSeR decouples closed-set recognition from open-set discovery by injecting relational knowledge from a lightweight, domain-adapted teacher model. This approach preserves the semantic geometry of foundation models while improving the coherence of novel category discovery, offering a plug-and-play solution for robust GCD.

key_metrics.primary_metric: State-of-the-art performance on six GCD benchmarks
key_metrics.baseline: GCD baselines using DINO and DINOv2 backbones

technical_breakdown.method: CloSeR uses a two-stage process: first, it trains a closed-set teacher with lightweight block-wise adapters on known-class data; second, it transfers knowledge via Unified Relational Distillation (URD) to the GCD student.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Frozen foundation model backbone (DINO/DINOv2), lightweight block-wise adapters for the teacher, and separate feature pathways for global (sample-to-prototype) and local (sample-to-sample) relational distillation.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Block-wise adapter tuning, Unified Relational Distillation (URD) with complementary global and local relations, head-agnostic integration with parametric and non-parametric GCD methods.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Low training cost due to frozen backbone and lightweight adapters; plug-and-play integration suggests minimal architectural overhead.

paper.title: Towards Purified Multi-Label Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
paper.summary: Test-time adaptation (TTA) has been widely explored in single-label recognition, effectively mitigating distribution shifts, especially when combined with vision-language models. However, real-world images often contain multiple objects, while the more practical multi-label test-time adaptation (MLTTA) has received little attention so far. Recent cache-based TTA methods have shown promising efficiency and effectiveness, yet directly extending them to multi-label scenarios suffers from a one-to-many mapping problem: a shared global representation entangling co-occurring objects is stored as class-wise cache prototypes, inducing dominant-label bias and compromised cache calibration. While introducing region-level cues helps isolate class-specific evidence, such regional evidence can also be unreliable under distribution shifts, making its identification and utilization non-trivial. To address these issues, we introduce PuRF, a novel PuRiFication-driven cache-based method for multi-label test-time adaptation of vision-language models. Specifically, PuRF first performs region purification to identify reliable regions, providing comprehensive regional cues for multi-label recognition and enabling fine-grained alignment. Based on these purified regions, PuRF conducts cache purification to enhance cache representation and adaptability, where episodic purification builds a discriminative region-based cache, and temporal refreshing further promotes long-term cache adaptability. Experiments demonstrate that PuRF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a notable 4.05% mAP improvement on ViT-B/32 across five datasets.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the challenge of extending cache-based test-time adaptation to multi-label recognition, where shared global representations cause dominant-label bias and unreliable regional evidence under distribution shifts.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Distribution shift in multi-label vision-language models, specifically the entanglement of co-occurring objects in global cache prototypes leading to calibration errors.
analysis.executive_summary: This work bridges the gap between single-label and multi-label test-time adaptation by introducing a purification mechanism that isolates reliable regional cues. It is significant for real-world applications where images contain multiple objects, as it mitigates the dominant-label bias inherent in standard cache-based TTA methods.

key_metrics.primary_metric: mAP improvement on ViT-B/32 across five datasets
key_metrics.baseline: State-of-the-art multi-label test-time adaptation methods

technical_breakdown.method: PuRF employs a two-stage purification strategy: first, region purification identifies reliable regions for fine-grained alignment; second, cache purification enhances representation through episodic purification (building discriminative region-based caches) and temporal refreshing (promoting long-term adaptability).
technical_breakdown.architecture: Vision-Language Model (ViT-B/32) backbone with a cache-based test-time adaptation module incorporating region-level cues and episodic/temporal cache management.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Region purification for identifying reliable evidence, episodic purification for discriminative cache construction, and temporal refreshing for cache adaptability.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not explicitly stated, but implies additional computational overhead for region identification and cache management compared to standard global cache TTA.

paper.title: Bootstrapping a 4D LiDAR Annotation Tool from Video Foundation Models
paper.summary: Progress in 4D LiDAR segmentation is bottlenecked by data. Assigning temporally consistent labels across sparse point cloud sequences is costly and hard to scale, and every new task or domain tends to demand fresh dense annotation. This motivates a simple question of whether high-quality LiDAR training data can be produced automatically, without any human labeling. To this end, we introduce LiDAR-SAM2, a framework that turns a 2D video foundation model, SAM2, into a scalable source of supervision for the 4D LiDAR domain. On the data side, it automatically generates temporally coherent LiDAR-level labels from SAM2 video masks through multi-view projection and spatio-temporal aggregation. On the modeling side, a tailored modality interface and a two-stage learning objective adapt SAM2's video segmentation kernel to spatio-temporal LiDAR structure, so that a single click per object yields a consistent mask track across the sequence. Trained with no human LiDAR annotation, LiDAR-SAM2 produces semantic and panoptic labels on SemanticKITTI that approach the quality of full human annotation from only a few points, and models trained on these labels approach the performance of full ground-truth supervision. This positions LiDAR-SAM2 as a scalable labeling tool that substantially reduces the annotation burden for 3D and 4D scene understanding.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the high cost and scalability limitations of manually annotating temporally consistent 4D LiDAR point cloud sequences for segmentation tasks.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Data annotation bottleneck in 3D/4D perception, specifically the scarcity of dense, temporally coherent ground-truth labels for sparse LiDAR data.
analysis.executive_summary: This work bridges the gap between 2D video foundation models and 3D LiDAR perception by automatically generating high-quality supervision without human labeling. It demonstrates that labels derived from SAM2 can train models that approach the performance of those trained on full human ground truth, significantly reducing the barrier to entry for new 4D LiDAR tasks and domains.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Performance of models trained on auto-generated labels vs. full human ground-truth supervision on SemanticKITTI
key_metrics.baseline: Full human annotation (ground truth)

technical_breakdown.method: The framework projects 2D video masks from SAM2 into the 3D LiDAR space using multi-view projection and spatio-temporal aggregation to create coherent LiDAR-level labels. It then adapts the SAM2 video segmentation kernel to LiDAR structure via a tailored modality interface and a two-stage learning objective.
technical_breakdown.architecture: LiDAR-SAM2 framework consisting of a data generation module (projection/aggregation) and a modeling module (modality interface + two-stage objective) built upon the SAM2 video foundation model.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Multi-view projection of 2D masks, spatio-temporal aggregation for temporal coherence, tailored modality interface for LiDAR, and a two-stage learning objective. Requires only a single click per object to generate consistent mask tracks.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not specified in summary

paper.title: Efficient Training with Foresight: Multi-Token Auxiliary Supervision for Autoregressive Image Generation
paper.summary: Autoregressive (AR) image generation has shown strong potential for scalable high-fidelity synthesis by modeling images as discrete token sequences. However, traditional next token prediction (NTP) continues to suffer from sparse and myopic supervision, insufficiently discriminative representations, and high training cost caused by dense computation over the full token sequence. To address these issues, we propose multi-token autoregressive (MTAR), a unified training framework that improves autoregressive image generation from three aspects: prediction objectives, representation regularization, and training efficiency. Specifically, MTAR introduces multi-token prediction (MTP) to alleviate the sparsity and myopia of traditional NTP by imposing joint supervision on multiple future tokens; employs token-level contrastive regularization (TCR) to explicitly enhance the separability of sampled token representations and thereby improve representation discriminability; and incorporates semantic dropping (SD) as a semantics-aware training acceleration strategy to reduce redundant computation on low-information tokens while preserving informative learning signals. All three components are applied only during training and introduce no additional overhead during autoregressive inference. On ImageNet, MTAR achieves a better balance between generation quality and training efficiency. Compared with LlamaGen, MTAR achieves up to 0.95 lower FID and 39\% faster training. Moreover, even with only 1/3 of the training iterations, it still attains performance comparable to or better than the baseline, substantially reducing training time.

analysis.problem_statement: Autoregressive image generation suffers from sparse and myopic supervision, insufficiently discriminative token representations, and high training costs due to dense computation over full token sequences.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Training efficiency and representation quality in autoregressive sequence modeling.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the high computational cost and limited representational power of standard next-token prediction in image generation. By introducing multi-token prediction, contrastive regularization, and semantic dropping, it significantly reduces training time while improving generation fidelity, offering a more scalable path for high-resolution image synthesis.

key_metrics.primary_metric: FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) and training speed
key_metrics.baseline: LlamaGen
key_metrics.improvement_percentage: 39% faster training; comparable performance with 1/3 training iterations

technical_breakdown.method: A unified training framework (MTAR) that combines multi-token prediction for joint supervision, token-level contrastive regularization for better representation separability, and semantic dropping to skip low-information tokens during training.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Autoregressive transformer-based image generation model with auxiliary supervision heads and regularization modules applied only during the training phase.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Multi-token prediction (MTP) imposes joint supervision on multiple future tokens; Token-level Contrastive Regularization (TCR) enhances separability of sampled token representations; Semantic Dropping (SD) reduces redundant computation on low-information tokens.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Training complexity is reduced by up to 39% compared to baseline; no additional overhead is introduced during autoregressive inference.

paper.title: CEDAR: Controlled and Event-Driven Demand Forecasting via Residual Decomposition
paper.summary: Forecasting in large-scale e-commerce marketplaces is increasingly required to support planning: merchants need to evaluate sales outcomes under future action sequences such as budget schedules, rather than passively predicting what happens next. However, most existing time series forecasting (TSF) approaches remain inherently passive. Even when incorporating operational decisions as auxiliary covariates, they typically optimize for correlation-based extrapolation under historical policies. This design suffers from autoregressive inertia and conflates endogenous market evolution with decision-induced transitions, leading to policy-insensitive rollouts and unreliable counterfactual analysis. To bridge this gap, we propose CEDAR (Controlled and Event-Driven Demand forecasting via Action-aware Residual decomposition), a two-stage framework for robust decision-conditioned simulation. In Stage I, an Action-Interleaved Transformer learns controllable action-conditioned state transitions for rollout under planned interventions. In Stage II, a Residual Correction Module leverages external event signals and LLM-assisted text representations to align noisy event descriptions with product context and correct event-driven deviations. Our study is enabled by a large-scale real-world dataset from Alibaba 1688, comprising approximately 32 million product trajectories with paired state-action sequences and aligned event signals. Extensive offline experiments and online controlled experiments in production demonstrate that CEDAR consistently improves simulation accuracy over strong TSF baselines and delivers practical gains for real-world budget planning.
paper.comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Published in KDD 2026

analysis.problem_statement: Existing time series forecasting models are passive and correlation-based, failing to accurately simulate demand under specific future action sequences (counterfactuals) by conflating endogenous market evolution with decision-induced transitions.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Lack of causal controllability and policy-sensitivity in standard time series forecasting models for counterfactual simulation.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the critical gap between passive prediction and active decision support in e-commerce by enabling robust, action-conditioned demand simulation. It is significant for the AI landscape as it moves beyond correlation-based extrapolation to provide reliable counterfactual analysis, which is essential for automated budget planning and resource allocation in large-scale marketplaces.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Simulation accuracy improvement over strong TSF baselines in offline and online controlled experiments.
key_metrics.baseline: Strong Time Series Forecasting (TSF) baselines

technical_breakdown.method: A two-stage framework: Stage I uses an Action-Interleaved Transformer to learn controllable state transitions for planned interventions; Stage II uses a Residual Correction Module to align external event signals and LLM-assisted text representations to correct event-driven deviations.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Action-Interleaved Transformer (Stage I) and Residual Correction Module (Stage II) incorporating LLM-assisted text representations.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Utilizes paired state-action sequences and aligned event signals from a 32-million product trajectory dataset; employs LLMs to process noisy event descriptions and align them with product context.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: High computational overhead due to the integration of LLM-assisted text representations and large-scale transformer training on 32 million trajectories.

paper.title: When RAG Fails to Equalize: Geo-bias in Factual Question Answering over Public Companies
paper.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is widely assumed to mitigate factual errors in large language models (LLMs), but it remains unclear whether retrieval uniformly compensates for missing knowledge. We study this question in a controlled factual QA setting over public companies, constructing a benchmark of approximately 2,000 firms across global equity indices. We evaluate six LLMs on four atomic attributes under four conditions: no-context, perfect context, misleading context, and distraction context. We find strong geographic disparities in no-context accuracy, indicating uneven parametric knowledge. While perfect context improves performance, it does not eliminate these gaps: gains are correlated with baseline accuracy, suggesting retrieval effectiveness is coupled to internal representations. Under misleading context, models frequently copy incorrect information. Larger models improve overall performance but do not remove these structural effects. These results challenge the view of RAG as a universal corrective and highlight the interaction between model knowledge, context quality, and entity representation.

analysis.problem_statement: This paper investigates whether Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) uniformly mitigates factual errors in Large Language Models (LLMs) or if geographic and entity-specific biases in parametric knowledge persist despite the provision of correct context.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Factual hallucination and uneven parametric knowledge distribution across entities and geographies in LLMs.
analysis.executive_summary: This study challenges the assumption that RAG acts as a universal corrective for factual errors by demonstrating that retrieval effectiveness is coupled to a model's internal representations. It reveals that geographic disparities in baseline knowledge persist even with perfect context, and that models are susceptible to copying incorrect information from misleading contexts. These findings highlight critical limitations in relying solely on RAG to ensure factual accuracy across diverse global entities.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Persistence of geographic accuracy disparities under perfect context conditions
key_metrics.metric_value: Not explicitly quantified in summary; qualitative finding of correlated gains with baseline accuracy
key_metrics.baseline: No-context (parametric only) accuracy across ~2,000 firms in global equity indices
key_metrics.improvement_percentage: N/A (Study focuses on structural effects and disparities rather than a single aggregate improvement metric)

technical_breakdown.method: Controlled factual QA evaluation using a constructed benchmark of ~2,000 public companies across global equity indices, testing four context conditions: no-context, perfect, misleading, and distraction.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Evaluation framework comparing six LLMs on four atomic attributes without modifying model architecture, focusing on the interaction between parametric knowledge and retrieved context.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Construction of a geographic benchmark; systematic variation of context quality (perfect, misleading, distraction); analysis of correlation between baseline accuracy and RAG gains.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: N/A (Evaluation study; computational cost depends on inference of six LLMs over ~2,000 entities x 4 attributes x 4 conditions).

paper.title: RA-VLA: Retrieval-Augmented VLA for Test-Time Adaptation
paper.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models provide a versatile foundation for general robotic manipulation, yet they exhibit significant brittleness when confronted with novel task distributions. While In-Context Imitation Learning (ICIL) offers a training-free alternative, existing frameworks suffer from an adaptation bottleneck that hinders the effective translation of expert context to executable actions. This failure originates from superficial retrieval mechanisms and an inherent behavioral inertia that anchors the policy to its pre-trained priors. To address these limitations, we present RA-VLA, a retrieval-augmented VLA framework that integrates behavior-aligned context retrieval with a grounded execution pipeline. By enforcing faithful adherence to functional cues within a scalable architecture, RA-VLA facilitates seamless task adaptation while preserving inference efficiency. Our empirical evaluations across the LIBERO benchmark and a real-world UR5e environment demonstrate that RA-VLA achieves superior success rates and computational efficiency, establishing a robust framework for training-free robotic adaptation.

analysis.problem_statement: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models suffer from brittleness and behavioral inertia when adapting to novel task distributions, causing existing In-Context Imitation Learning frameworks to fail in translating expert context into executable actions.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Test-time adaptation and distribution shift in robotic manipulation policies without requiring additional training.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the critical limitation of VLA models in generalizing to unseen tasks by introducing a retrieval-augmented framework that overcomes the 'adaptation bottleneck' of current training-free methods. By decoupling context retrieval from execution through behavior-aligned mechanisms, it enables robust, real-time adaptation in both simulation and physical environments.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Success rate and computational efficiency in robotic manipulation tasks
key_metrics.baseline: Existing In-Context Imitation Learning (ICIL) frameworks

technical_breakdown.method: Integrates behavior-aligned context retrieval with a grounded execution pipeline to enforce faithful adherence to functional cues, thereby overcoming superficial retrieval and behavioral inertia.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Retrieval-Augmented VLA framework consisting of a scalable retrieval module and a grounded execution pipeline.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses behavior-aligned context retrieval to map expert demonstrations to executable actions, preserving pre-trained priors while allowing seamless task adaptation.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Training-free approach designed to preserve inference efficiency, implying low computational overhead during adaptation compared to fine-tuning methods.

paper.title: VGA-BenchV2: An Expanded Unified Benchmark and Multi-Model Framework for Evaluating Video Aesthetics and Generation Quality
paper.summary: We introduce VGA-BenchV2, an extended human-aligned benchmark and optimization framework for jointly evaluating and improving video generation quality and aesthetic value. Built upon VGA-Bench, VGA-BenchV2 preserves the original fine-grained taxonomy with two primary dimensions-Aesthetic and Generation-and 52 sub-dimensions. Guided by this taxonomy, we curate 1,016 diverse prompts and collect over 60,000 videos generated by 12 mainstream video generation models. More importantly, VGA-BenchV2 substantially expands human-labeled supervision by adding 36,000 task-level annotations, including 16,200 for aesthetic quality, 13,200 for aesthetic tagging, and 6,600 for generation quality, corresponding to 13.46x, 11.15x, and 1.55x scale-ups over VGA-Bench, respectively. Leveraging this enlarged annotation corpus, we develop a hybrid evaluator architecture consisting of VAQA-Net for continuous aesthetic scoring and two Qwen-based Large Vision-Language Model evaluators, VTag-Net and VGQA-Net, for aesthetic tagging and generation quality assessment. Extensive experiments demonstrate strong alignment with human judgments across diverse generation models. Beyond evaluation, VGA-BenchV2 further introduces an evaluation-to-optimization pipeline, where the learned aesthetic evaluator serves as a reward model for reinforcement learning-based generator fine-tuning. This closes the loop from benchmark construction and human supervision to automated evaluation and model optimization, enabling video generators to improve not only in realism but also in aesthetic quality and human preference alignment. Resources are available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/BestiVictoryLab/VGA-Bench.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the lack of a sufficiently large, human-aligned benchmark and integrated optimization framework for jointly evaluating and improving both the aesthetic quality and technical generation fidelity of video generation models.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Scarcity of high-quality, fine-grained human supervision data for video aesthetics and the disconnect between evaluation benchmarks and model optimization pipelines.
analysis.executive_summary: VGA-BenchV2 significantly expands the supervision signal for video generation evaluation by scaling human annotations by up to 13.46x over its predecessor, enabling more robust alignment with human preferences. By integrating a hybrid evaluator architecture with a reinforcement learning-based fine-tuning pipeline, it bridges the gap between static benchmarking and active model improvement, allowing generators to optimize for both realism and aesthetic value simultaneously.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Scale-up of human-labeled supervision data compared to VGA-Bench
key_metrics.metric_value: 36,000 total annotations (16,200 aesthetic quality, 13,200 aesthetic tagging, 6,600 generation quality)
key_metrics.baseline: VGA-Bench

technical_breakdown.method: A unified framework that curates a diverse prompt set, collects videos from 12 mainstream models, and uses a hybrid evaluator to score aesthetics and generation quality, which then serves as a reward model for RL-based generator fine-tuning.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Hybrid evaluator consisting of VAQA-Net (continuous aesthetic scoring) and two Qwen-based Large Vision-Language Models (VTag-Net for tagging, VGQA-Net for generation quality), coupled with an evaluation-to-optimization pipeline using reinforcement learning.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Utilizes 1,016 diverse prompts and over 60,000 generated videos. The optimization phase uses the learned aesthetic evaluator as a reward model to fine-tune video generators via reinforcement learning, closing the loop from evaluation to improvement.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: High computational overhead due to the generation of 60,000+ videos and the training of multiple large vision-language models (Qwen-based) alongside the RL fine-tuning process.

paper.title: CRAMER: Control via Request-Aware Masking for Editing Recommenders
paper.summary: Sequential recommendation models, while powerful, have limited flexibility in responding to immediate user requests, making it difficult to adapt their recommendations to the user's timely interests. Unfortunately, existing user request adaptation methods often incur high computational overhead due to either 1) retraining the entire backbone network or 2) leveraging the inference ability of large language models (a.k.a. prompt engineering), limiting their applicability in large-scale recommendation services. This paper presents Control via Request-Aware Masking for Editing Recommenders (CRAMER), a framework that takes users' natural-language requests to immediately change sequential recommendation models' behavior. Specifically, inspired by the model control theory, CRAMER treats user requests as control signals to modulate frozen backbone parameters through masking, achieving instant adaptation to diverse requests while avoiding costly retraining. Experiments on multiple large-scale benchmark datasets show that CRAMER outperforms four state-of-the-art request-aware baselines across multiple recommendation metrics while achieving minimal overhead. Moreover, the proposed framework exhibits enhanced controllability and cross-domain adaptability, establishing a new paradigm for request-aware sequential recommendation.

analysis.problem_statement: Existing methods for adapting sequential recommendation models to immediate user natural-language requests suffer from high computational overhead due to full retraining or reliance on large language model inference.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: High computational latency and cost associated with real-time model adaptation and inference in large-scale recommendation systems.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the scalability bottleneck in request-aware recommendation by eliminating the need for expensive retraining or LLM inference during adaptation. By using request-aware masking to modulate frozen backbone parameters, it enables instant, low-overhead control of recommendation behavior, making real-time personalization feasible for large-scale industrial services.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Outperformance across multiple recommendation metrics with minimal overhead
key_metrics.baseline: Four state-of-the-art request-aware baselines

technical_breakdown.method: Treats user natural-language requests as control signals to modulate frozen backbone parameters via masking, inspired by model control theory.
technical_breakdown.architecture: A framework that interfaces with a frozen sequential recommendation backbone, applying dynamic masks based on request inputs to alter model behavior without weight updates.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Request-Aware Masking mechanism that maps natural language requests to specific parameter modulation patterns.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Minimal inference overhead compared to retraining or LLM-based methods; avoids costly retraining cycles.

paper.title: RTLGuard: A Lightweight Teacher-Student Defense for Poisoned RTL Code Generation Models
paper.summary: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) is driving a shift toward automated register transfer level (RTL) code generation, enabling designers to translate high-level specs. into synthesizable hardware. However, this reliance on pre-trained (3rd-party) fine-tuned models may introduce critical trust issues, as the training data and adaptation process of these models are often opaque. Thus, adversaries (even model providers) may embed hidden backdoor threats during fine-tuning, allowing malicious behavior, e.g., hardware Trojans, to be triggered by seemingly benign prompts given by victim user at inference time. In this paper, we introduce RTLGuard, to mitigate such a trust issue in AI-enabled IC supply chain. Rather than prohibitive computational cost of full-parameter retraining, RTLGuard leverages a teacher-student framework designed to sanitize compromised RTL generation models by (1) fine-tuning a small-scale, "clean" teacher model on a limited set of trusted RTL data, (2) guiding the poisoned target model via a composite teacher-student objective, and (3) incorporating feature alignment and knowledge distillation to suppress malicious behaviors. Our experiments across various LLM architectures demonstrate that RTLGuard significantly reduces the Attack Success Rate (ASR) while preserving the functional correctness and synthesizability of the generated RTL code.
paper.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 7 tables. Accepted at the IEEE/ACM International Conference on Computer-Aided Design (ICCAD 2026)

analysis.problem_statement: Pre-trained and fine-tuned LLMs for RTL code generation may contain hidden backdoors or hardware Trojans introduced by untrusted third-party providers, posing critical security risks to the IC supply chain.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Trust and security in third-party AI models, specifically the lack of transparency in training data and fine-tuning processes that allows for adversarial backdoor injection.
analysis.executive_summary: As hardware design increasingly relies on automated RTL generation, the opacity of third-party model fine-tuning creates a vector for malicious backdoors that can trigger hardware Trojans. This paper addresses the high computational cost of full retraining by proposing a lightweight sanitization method, ensuring that compromised models can be made safe without prohibitive resource expenditure.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Reduction in Attack Success Rate (ASR) while maintaining functional correctness and synthesizability
key_metrics.baseline: Poisoned target models (pre-sanitization)

technical_breakdown.method: A teacher-student framework that sanitizes a poisoned target model by using a small, clean teacher model fine-tuned on trusted data to guide the target via a composite objective.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Teacher model (small-scale, clean, fine-tuned on trusted RTL data), Student model (the poisoned target LLM), and a composite objective function incorporating feature alignment and knowledge distillation.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Fine-tuning a small teacher on limited trusted data; applying a composite teacher-student objective to the poisoned model; using feature alignment and knowledge distillation to suppress malicious behaviors.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Lightweight compared to full-parameter retraining; leverages a small-scale teacher model to reduce computational overhead.

paper.title: APT: Accelerating Diffusion Transformers via Attention Probability-Guided Pruning and Quantization
paper.summary: Recent advances in generative AI have significantly increased the demand for high-resolution image and video generation, positioning diffusion models as a core technology. Among them, Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have emerged as the state-of-the-art (SOTA) models due to their scalability and output quality. However, self-attention in DiTs incurs significant computational overhead, leading to excessively long latency as the complexity grows with the fourth power of the output resolution. While prior works have attempted to mitigate this cost using sparsity and quantization techniques, they fall short of effectively reducing the computational cost in high-resolution DiTs.   In this paper, we present APT, a software-hardware co-designed accelerator for high-resolution DiTs. APT leverages attention probabilities as a unified importance metric to jointly optimize computation through fine-grained pruning and adaptive precision scaling. At the algorithm level, we propose Attention Probability-guided Adaptive Dual Thresholding (APDT), which dynamically performs element selection and precision assignment using dual thresholds. To ensure compatibility with memory-efficient FlashAttention, we introduce Timestep-Aware FlashAttention (TAFA), which predicts attention probabilities across timesteps by exploiting temporal similarity. At the architecture level, we co-design a specialized accelerator that efficiently supports irregular sparsity and dual-precision execution, featuring dynamic mask management, address translation, dual-precision compute units, and a tile-based dataflow. Finally, we evaluate APT on SOTA DiT models, including PixArt-$α$, Stable Diffusion 3, and FLUX. APT achieves up to 8.16$\times$ speedup and 14.98$\times$ higher energy efficiency over NVIDIA A100, and up to 3.01$\times$ speedup and 2.04$\times$ higher energy efficiency over EXION, a SOTA diffusion model accelerator.
paper.comment: 9 pages, 17 figures, 3 tables. Accepted to the IEEE/ACM International Conference on Computer-Aided Design (ICCAD 2026)

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the excessive computational latency and energy consumption of self-attention mechanisms in high-resolution Diffusion Transformers (DiTs), where complexity scales with the fourth power of output resolution.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Computational efficiency and energy efficiency of self-attention in high-resolution generative models.
analysis.executive_summary: This work is significant because it provides a software-hardware co-designed solution to the scaling bottleneck of state-of-the-art Diffusion Transformers, which are central to modern high-resolution image and video generation. By unifying pruning and quantization via attention probabilities, it enables efficient deployment on specialized hardware, overcoming the limitations of prior sparsity and quantization methods that fail to reduce costs effectively at high resolutions.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Speedup and Energy Efficiency
key_metrics.baseline: NVIDIA A100
key_metrics.improvement_percentage: 716% speedup and 1398% energy efficiency improvement over A100

technical_breakdown.method: APT uses attention probabilities as a unified importance metric to jointly optimize computation through fine-grained pruning and adaptive precision scaling, implemented via a software-hardware co-design approach.
technical_breakdown.architecture: A specialized accelerator featuring dynamic mask management, address translation, dual-precision compute units, and a tile-based dataflow to support irregular sparsity and dual-precision execution.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Utilizes Attention Probability-guided Adaptive Dual Thresholding (APDT) for element selection and precision assignment, and Timestep-Aware FlashAttention (TAFA) to predict attention probabilities across timesteps for compatibility with memory-efficient FlashAttention.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Reduces computational overhead of self-attention which normally grows with the fourth power of output resolution; specific training times are not provided, but inference latency is significantly reduced.

paper.title: Gaming Together on Discord: Teen Gamer's Cross-Platform Practices
paper.summary: Discord is one of the most popular communication platforms among gamers. While prior research has highlighted its role in community building, relatively little attention has been paid to its original gaming context-how it shapes gameplay and social experiences. To address this gap, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 16 teenage Discord users. Through reflexive thematic analysis, we show how players leverage Discord to create more collaborative and socially enriched experiences that extend beyond the game itself. However, gaming together on Discord also resulted in social and security risks. We conceptualize gaming together on Discord as a cross-platform practice that extends gameplay beyond a game and supports players' social needs. Additionally, cross-platform practice also introduces the 'platform gap,' where fragmented governance between platforms exposed players to risks. To address this tension, we propose design implications aimed at bridging the platform gap, strengthening communication channels, and supporting safer gaming experiences.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the lack of understanding regarding how Discord functions as a cross-platform practice that shapes gameplay and social experiences for teenage gamers, while simultaneously introducing security and governance risks due to fragmented platform oversight.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: This paper does not address an AI bottleneck; it is a Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) study focusing on social dynamics, user behavior, and platform design.
analysis.executive_summary: This research is relevant to the AI landscape primarily through its implications for the design of AI-mediated social spaces and safety mechanisms in gaming platforms. It highlights the 'platform gap' where fragmented governance across gaming and communication platforms exposes users to risks, a challenge that AI safety and moderation systems must navigate. The findings provide a framework for designing AI-assisted tools that support social needs while mitigating cross-platform security vulnerabilities.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Qualitative identification of cross-platform practices and the 'platform gap' concept
key_metrics.baseline: Prior research focusing on community building rather than gameplay context

technical_breakdown.method: Semi-structured interviews with teenage Discord users followed by reflexive thematic analysis.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Not applicable; this is a qualitative social science study, not a system architecture.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Reflexive thematic analysis used to code interview data and identify themes related to collaborative gameplay, social enrichment, and security risks.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not applicable

paper.title: UltraPIPS: Improving model perception in B-mode ultrasound with foundation models
paper.summary: In medical imaging, it is common to use learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) to compare images semantically in feature space. Although backbones pretrained on natural images are widely used for LPIPS computation, B-mode ultrasound images possess distinct speckle patterns and acoustic-specific image statistics that are fundamentally different from natural images and even from other images in radiology. Consequently, we propose that domain-specific models are needed to measure perceptual similarity in ultrasound data, a finding which is not necessarily the case for other imaging modalities. We compare LPIPS metrics across downstream tasks like classification, segmentation and reconstruction using natural image, medical generalist and ultrasound backbone models and show that selection of LPIPS backbone is a non-trivial design choice. In particular, the ultrasound backbone models were more correlated with downstream performance of supervised models than classical and natural image models, and optimization of the LPIPS loss with an ultrasound backbone achieved a strong balance between reconstruction quality and realism. Our code is available at https://github.com/talg2324/UltraPIPS and introduces the UltraPIPS library, a set of LPIPS metrics based on the open-source foundation models analyzed in this paper.

analysis.problem_statement: Standard LPIPS metrics based on natural image backbones fail to accurately capture perceptual similarity in B-mode ultrasound due to domain-specific speckle patterns and acoustic statistics.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Domain gap in perceptual loss functions for specialized medical imaging modalities.
analysis.executive_summary: The paper demonstrates that using generic natural image or generalist medical models for LPIPS computation is suboptimal for ultrasound, as these models do not align with the unique statistical properties of B-mode images. By introducing UltraPIPS, a library of LPIPS metrics based on ultrasound-specific foundation models, the authors show improved correlation with downstream task performance and better balance between reconstruction quality and realism.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Correlation with downstream supervised model performance and balance of reconstruction quality/realism
key_metrics.baseline: LPIPS metrics using natural image and generalist medical backbone models

technical_breakdown.method: Comparison of LPIPS metrics derived from different backbone models (natural, medical generalist, ultrasound-specific) across classification, segmentation, and reconstruction tasks.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Utilizes open-source foundation models as backbones for feature extraction to compute perceptual similarity in feature space.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Development of the UltraPIPS library, which encapsulates LPIPS metrics based on analyzed ultrasound foundation models.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not specified in abstract

paper.title: LUTSeg: A Longitudinal Multi-Expert Dataset for Ulcer Tissue Segmentation
paper.summary: Quantifying wound tissue composition is essential for monitoring chronic ulcer progression and guiding treatment decisions. However, pixel-level annotations are costly, and multi-tissue wound datasets remain scarce, particularly for neglected diseases such as leprosy. We introduce LUTSeg, a longitudinal chronic ulcer dataset comprising 141 images from 39 patients with wound masks and five tissue categories annotated by five expert clinicians, including a multi-expert gold-standard subset for inter-rater agreement analysis. To establish an initial benchmark for LUTSeg, we further propose TiSage, a semi-supervised tissue segmentation framework that integrates multi-scale semantic priors from a frozen medical vision-language model within a teacher-student architecture. We evaluate TiSage on LUTSeg and DFUTissue, showing improvements over supervised and semi-supervised baselines in most low-label settings. Code & data: https://github.com/carlosh93/TiSage

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the scarcity of pixel-level annotated multi-tissue datasets for chronic ulcers, particularly for neglected diseases like leprosy, which hinders the development of accurate wound segmentation models.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Data scarcity and high annotation cost for pixel-level multi-class segmentation in medical imaging.
analysis.executive_summary: This work introduces LUTSeg, a longitudinal multi-expert dataset for chronic ulcer segmentation, and TiSage, a semi-supervised framework that leverages frozen medical vision-language models to reduce annotation dependency. It provides a critical benchmark for low-label settings in wound care AI, addressing a gap in neglected disease research.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Segmentation performance in low-label settings
key_metrics.baseline: Supervised and semi-supervised baselines on LUTSeg and DFUTissue

technical_breakdown.method: TiSage is a semi-supervised tissue segmentation framework that integrates multi-scale semantic priors from a frozen medical vision-language model within a teacher-student architecture.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Teacher-student architecture with a frozen medical vision-language model providing multi-scale semantic priors.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses longitudinal data from 39 patients (141 images) with 5 tissue categories; includes a multi-expert gold-standard subset for inter-rater agreement analysis.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not specified; code available at https://github.com/carlosh93/TiSage

paper.title: Steer the Sampling, Not the Kernel Grid: Geometry-Guided Sampling Operator for Volumetric Segmentation
paper.summary: Accurate 3D segmentation is central to quantitative lesion assessment and anatomy mapping for clinical planning and follow-up. Thin, elongated, and fine anatomical/pathological structures (e.g., vessels) are a particularly challenging case: a one-voxel boundary error can disconnect a branch and change clinically relevant topology. In encoder-decoder networks (e.g., U-Net), repeated downsampling and fixed-grid convolution blur or alias fine structures and weaken orientation cues, so early mistakes propagate across scales. We propose a geometry-guided local operator that steers where features are sampled, rather than deforming convolutional kernels, under a single formulation for both feature refinement (stride 1) and resolution reduction (stride > 1). At each voxel, it predicts a local orientation and bounded step sizes, samples symmetrically along these directions, and transforms paired samples into compact geometric and boundary cues with lightweight mixing; a cross-scale consensus aligns encoder and decoder features at skip connections to reduce geometric mismatch. Replacing all stride 1 and stride 2 operators in a 3D U-Net yields consistent improvements on BraTS, MSD Hepatic Vessel, and TDSC-ABUS, with notably better boundary metrics (e.g., BraTS Dice 86.1 to 88.9, HD95 7.1 to 6.2; TDSC-ABUS HD95 39.1 to 27.8) while reducing parameters from 2.3M to 0.8M. We further demonstrate that the operator can be integrated into other backbones (e.g., nnU-Net, Swin-UNETR, and MedNeXt) without changing their macro-architectures while providing consistent performance gains.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the degradation of fine, thin anatomical structures (like vessels) in 3D volumetric segmentation caused by fixed-grid convolutions and downsampling in encoder-decoder networks, which leads to topological errors and boundary blurring.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Spatial resolution loss and aliasing in fixed-grid convolutional operations during downsampling and feature refinement.
analysis.executive_summary: This work introduces a geometry-guided sampling operator that replaces standard convolutions by steering feature sampling directions based on local orientation, rather than deforming kernels. It significantly improves boundary accuracy and topological consistency for thin structures while reducing model parameter count, offering a drop-in replacement for standard U-Net components.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Dice Coefficient on BraTS dataset
key_metrics.baseline: Standard 3D U-Net (Dice 86.1)

technical_breakdown.method: A local operator predicts orientation and bounded step sizes at each voxel to sample features symmetrically along these directions, transforming paired samples into geometric and boundary cues via lightweight mixing.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Geometry-guided local operator integrated into 3D U-Net, nnU-Net, Swin-UNETR, and MedNeXt backbones, replacing stride 1 and stride 2 operators; includes cross-scale consensus alignment at skip connections.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Predicts local orientation and step sizes; samples symmetrically; uses lightweight mixing for geometric/boundary cues; cross-scale consensus aligns encoder/decoder features.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Reduces parameters from 2.3M to 0.8M in the tested 3D U-Net configuration, implying lower computational overhead for the replaced modules.

paper.title: Label-Free Foundational Model Selection for Medical Image Classification under Distribution Shift via Pseudo Label Discrepancy
paper.summary: Foundation models are increasingly deployed for medical image analysis. However, under the inter-institutional distribution shift typical of deployment, their performance varies widely and cannot be known without target-domain labels, which are rarely available. This leaves a practical question unresolved: given several candidate foundational models and labeled-data from a source domain, which one to deploy in an unlabeled target domain? We propose a label-free selection criterion built on SUDO, a framework for evaluating clinical AI systems without ground-truth annotations. SUDO partitions the unlabeled target data by predicted probability and, for each region, measures a pseudo-label discrepancy reflecting class contamination; aggregated across regions, this yields a score (AURCC) requiring neither target annotation nor fine-tuning. We show that AURCC can be used to rank a variety of vision-language models (BioMedCLIP, CXR-CLIP, CheXzero, MedCLIP, MedImageInsight, CLIP) on chest X-ray classification across three inter-hospital shift scenarios, under zero-shot and MLP-probe regimes. The AURCC ranking recovers the ground-truth ranking with Spearman rho up to 0.943 (p<0.05). Against the natural baseline of ranking by held-out source accuracy, AURCC is competitive when the labeled source is large and yields a more accurate ranking once it is small; the regime of interest in resource-constrained settings.
paper.comment: Accepted at MIRASOL Workshop, MICCAI 2026. 10 pages, 3 figures

analysis.problem_statement: How to select the optimal foundational model for medical image classification in an unlabeled target domain suffering from distribution shift, without requiring target-domain labels or fine-tuning.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Data scarcity and distribution shift in deployment environments where ground-truth annotations are unavailable.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the critical challenge of deploying foundation models in real-world medical settings where data distributions vary across institutions and labels are scarce. By introducing a label-free selection criterion (AURCC) based on pseudo-label discrepancy, it enables reliable model ranking without target annotations. This is particularly valuable for resource-constrained settings where labeled source data is limited, offering a practical solution for clinical AI deployment.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Ranking accuracy of candidate models against ground-truth performance
key_metrics.baseline: Ranking by held-out source accuracy
key_metrics.improvement_percentage: Not explicitly quantified as a percentage, but AURCC yields more accurate ranking than source accuracy when labeled source data is small.

technical_breakdown.method: The method uses the SUDO framework to partition unlabeled target data by predicted probability. For each region, it measures pseudo-label discrepancy reflecting class contamination. These discrepancies are aggregated into a score called AURCC (Area Under the Risk-Confidence Curve), which requires no target annotation or fine-tuning.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Vision-language models (BioMedCLIP, CXR-CLIP, CheXzero, MedCLIP, MedImageInsight, CLIP) are evaluated using the SUDO framework. The architecture involves probability-based partitioning of target data and discrepancy measurement across regions.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: The algorithm involves zero-shot and MLP-probe regimes. It calculates AURCC by aggregating pseudo-label discrepancies across probability-partitioned regions of the target domain. The method is applied to chest X-ray classification across three inter-hospital shift scenarios.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: The method is computationally efficient as it does not require fine-tuning or target-domain labels. It relies on inference from pre-trained models and simple aggregation of probability-based metrics, making it suitable for resource-constrained environments.
