paper.title: Learning What to Share and What to Personalize: Hierarchical Strategy Co-Evolution for Agent Memory
paper.summary: Memory-augmented agents maintain compact user profiles throughout extended conversations, enabling personalized and consistent responses without the need to process the entire dialogue history. The quality of these user profiles relies on the underlying memory management strategy: at each step, the agent must determine what to retain, compress, or discard. However, existing methods typically employ a static, one-size-fits-all strategy established before training. In practice, the optimal memory decision is inherently user-specific and dynamically evolves alongside policy optimization. To address this, we propose \textbf{HiPS} (\textbf{Hi}erarchical \textbf{P}ersonalized \textbf{S}trategy), a framework that decouples memory management into a globally shared foundation and a user-specific adaptive tier. Specifically, HiPS employs \textbf{Universal Strategy} to extract shared principles from cross-persona trajectories, alongside \textbf{Persona Delta Distillation} to generate tailored rules for users whose behaviors diverge from general patterns. \textbf{Cross-Level Rule Flow} dynamically calibrates their boundary by promoting broadly validated personal rules and demoting contradicted global ones. The architecture establishes a co-evolution loop where a mechanism guarantees that all strategy refinements are anchored to task outcomes. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements over memory-augmented baselines.

analysis.problem_statement: Existing memory-augmented agents use static, one-size-fits-all memory management strategies that fail to adapt to user-specific behavioral divergences and dynamic policy evolution.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Inefficiency and lack of personalization in long-context state management and memory retention strategies for LLM agents.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the rigidity of current agent memory systems by introducing a hierarchical framework that separates universal memory principles from user-specific adaptations. By enabling the co-evolution of these strategies based on task outcomes, it allows agents to maintain compact, high-quality user profiles without processing entire dialogue histories, thereby improving consistency and personalization in extended interactions.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Consistent improvements over memory-augmented baselines
key_metrics.baseline: Memory-augmented baselines

technical_breakdown.method: HiPS decouples memory management into a globally shared foundation and a user-specific adaptive tier, using a co-evolution loop anchored to task outcomes.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Hierarchical Strategy Co-Evolution framework comprising Universal Strategy, Persona Delta Distillation, and Cross-Level Rule Flow components.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Universal Strategy extracts shared principles from cross-persona trajectories; Persona Delta Distillation generates tailored rules for divergent users; Cross-Level Rule Flow dynamically calibrates boundaries by promoting validated personal rules and demoting contradicted global ones.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not specified in abstract

paper.title: A Training-Free Proactive Defense Against Partial Speech Manipulation via Self-Embedding Steganography
paper.summary: Partial deepfake speech, where only limited segments of an utterance are synthesized or manipulated, poses a significant challenge to existing deepfake detection systems. As the proportion of spoofed regions decreases, passive detectors become increasingly unreliable, and accurate detection and restoration remain challenging. In this paper, we revisit audio steganography from a new perspective and propose its use as a proactive defense against partially deepfaked audio. In particular, we consider a self-embedding strategy in which a clean speech signal embeds a compressed representation of itself, enabling post-hoc extraction of reference content. We demonstrate how existing audio steganography methods can be repurposed to support detection of partial deepfakes through codec-based restoration. Experiments on a benchmark dataset show that the proposed approach complements passive defenses. Remarkably, the proposed method operates without any training, providing a robust and data-efficient alternative for partial deepfake detection.
paper.comment: 6 pages; 4 figures; 1 tables; accepted at Interspeech 2026

analysis.problem_statement: Existing passive deepfake detection systems become unreliable when only small segments of a speech utterance are manipulated, making accurate detection and restoration of partial deepfakes difficult.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Reliability of passive detection mechanisms in low-spoof-ratio scenarios and the high data/training requirements of traditional deep learning-based defense models.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper proposes a training-free, proactive defense mechanism that leverages self-embedding audio steganography to embed a compressed reference of clean speech, enabling robust detection and restoration of partial deepfakes. It addresses the critical gap where passive detectors fail as the proportion of spoofed audio decreases, offering a data-efficient alternative that complements existing passive defenses without requiring model retraining.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Complementarity to passive defenses and robustness in partial deepfake detection
key_metrics.baseline: Existing passive deepfake detection systems

technical_breakdown.method: The method employs a self-embedding steganography strategy where a clean speech signal embeds a compressed representation of itself. This embedded reference allows for post-hoc extraction and comparison to detect manipulations, utilizing codec-based restoration to recover the original content.
technical_breakdown.architecture: No neural network architecture is proposed; the system relies on repurposed existing audio steganography methods and codec-based restoration pipelines.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Utilizes self-embedding of compressed speech representations; leverages standard audio steganography algorithms for embedding and extraction; applies codec-based techniques for restoration.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Training-free operation implies zero training time and low computational overhead associated with model inference, focusing instead on the computational cost of steganographic embedding/extraction and codec processing.

paper.title: Routed Graph Handoff: Adaptive Format Selection for Multi-Agent LLM Delegation
paper.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems coordinate through natural-language messages that consume 40--60\% of their token budget. Replacing these with structured graphs reduces cost but fails on tasks requiring adaptive reasoning. We propose \textbf{Routed Graph Handoff}, where a lightweight LLM router (155 tokens, 0.15\% overhead) selects between a typed dependency graph and natural language for each delegation. On four benchmarks (1,050+ trajectories), the routed system matches or exceeds NL-only on every task: \textbf{+12.7\,pp} on $τ$-retail at 3.2$\times$ compression ($p{<}0.01$), \textbf{+8.7\,pp} on BrowseComp at 2.2$\times$ compression ($p{<}0.05$), and parity on BFCL and AppWorld. Without the router, graph-only delegation regresses 14.6\,pp on AppWorld; the router eliminates this at near-zero cost. A graph-aware executor prompt is required: the same schema without interpretation guidance yields no gain. An oracle analysis reveals 8.6\,pp of additional headroom, motivating execution-time adaptive routing as future work.

analysis.problem_statement: Multi-agent LLM systems suffer from high token consumption (40-60% of budget) due to natural language coordination, while rigid structured graph delegation fails on tasks requiring adaptive reasoning.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Inefficient token utilization and lack of adaptability in inter-agent communication protocols.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the critical cost-efficiency trade-off in multi-agent LLM systems by introducing a lightweight router that dynamically selects between natural language and structured graph formats for delegation. It demonstrates that adaptive format selection can achieve significant cost compression (up to 3.2x) while maintaining or improving task performance, solving the rigidity issues of static structured communication.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Performance improvement on tau-retail benchmark with token compression
key_metrics.baseline: Natural Language (NL)-only delegation

technical_breakdown.method: A lightweight LLM router (155 tokens) evaluates each delegation step to select between a typed dependency graph and natural language, paired with a graph-aware executor prompt.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Router-Executor architecture where the router selects the communication format and the executor processes the message using format-specific interpretation guidance.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses a 155-token router prompt (0.15% overhead) and requires specific interpretation guidance in the executor prompt to realize gains from the graph schema.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Negligible overhead (0.15%) for routing; computational cost is dominated by the underlying LLM inference for the router and executor.

paper.title: Groundhog Bit-Flip Attack: Seeding Infinite Generation Loops in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs through Bit Flips
paper.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures enable scalable and efficient large language models (LLMs) by selectively activating expert sub-networks through a routing mechanism. However, this adaptive design introduces a new attack surface: specific experts become disproportionately correlated with certain tokens (e.g., end-of-sequence), allowing adversaries to manipulate model behavior via lightweight perturbations. In this work, we present \textbf{Groundhog Bit-Flip Attack (GBFA)}, the first bit-flip-based \textit{ Denial-of-Wallet availability attack} against MoE-based LLMs. By identifying and flipping routing-layer bits associated with related expert activations, we demonstrate that GBFA substantially extends the decoding token usage across three different LLM modes: conversational, reasoning, and agentic tasks, while largely preserving semantic fidelity. Across four main real-world MoE-based LLMs, manually deactivating on average fewer than \textbf{4 experts} drives average output inflation to $\mathbf{5912\%}$, with the majority of test samples reaching max tokens. These results reveal a robustness vulnerability of MoE architectures to bit flip, and highlight the potential of GBFA as an availability attack against LLMs.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the lack of robustness in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs against bit-flip perturbations that can trigger infinite generation loops, leading to denial-of-service or denial-of-wallet attacks.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Model robustness and security against physical or adversarial bit-level perturbations in inference.
analysis.executive_summary: This work reveals a critical vulnerability in MoE architectures where minimal bit-flips in routing layers can disproportionately activate specific experts, causing models to enter infinite generation loops. By demonstrating that deactivating fewer than 4 experts can inflate output tokens by over 5900%, the study highlights a significant availability risk for MoE-based LLMs in production environments.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Average output inflation percentage due to bit-flip attack
key_metrics.baseline: Standard MoE LLM inference without bit-flip perturbations

technical_breakdown.method: The Groundhog Bit-Flip Attack (GBFA) identifies routing-layer bits correlated with specific expert activations (e.g., end-of-sequence tokens) and flips them to manipulate the routing mechanism, forcing the model to select experts that promote continued generation rather than termination.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Large Language Models, specifically targeting the routing/gating mechanism and expert sub-networks.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: The attack involves manually deactivating on average fewer than 4 experts by flipping specific bits in the routing layer, which disrupts the normal termination logic and extends decoding across conversational, reasoning, and agentic modes.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Low computational overhead for the attacker, as it requires only lightweight bit-level perturbations to the model weights or routing parameters, not retraining or complex gradient-based optimization.

paper.title: DESCENT: Directed Edge Scene Encoding for Airport Surface Movement Prediction
paper.summary: Advanced automation is a key technology for enhancing the safety of ground operations amidst the increasing density of commercial air traffic. While motion forecasting is a well-studied task in autonomous driving, its application to airport surface movements remains underexplored. To enable efficient and accurate prediction in this domain, we propose DESCENT, a transformer-based architecture designed to handle heterogeneous dynamics and strict topological constraints. Our approach features a Potential Reachable Set (PRS) context sampling mechanism that adaptively collects airfield environment context across diverse operational phases. Combined with a detection transformer-based decoder, DESCENT generates accurate trajectory forecasts. Extensive evaluations on the Amelia-10 benchmark demonstrate significant performance improvements over state-of-the-art baselines. These gains are especially pronounced in safety-critical scenarios, where our domain-aware sampling provides critical long-horizon context necessary for safe navigation.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately predicting airport surface movements by handling heterogeneous vehicle dynamics and strict topological constraints that are underexplored in existing motion forecasting models.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Lack of domain-specific context sampling and architectural adaptation for topologically constrained, heterogeneous multi-agent environments in non-roadway settings.
analysis.executive_summary: This work extends motion forecasting from autonomous driving to airport surface operations, a critical domain for safety and efficiency. By introducing a domain-aware sampling mechanism that adapts to diverse operational phases, it provides the long-horizon context necessary for safe navigation in safety-critical scenarios.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Performance improvements over state-of-the-art baselines on the Amelia-10 benchmark, particularly in safety-critical scenarios.
key_metrics.baseline: State-of-the-art baselines on Amelia-10

technical_breakdown.method: A transformer-based architecture that utilizes a Potential Reachable Set (PRS) context sampling mechanism to adaptively collect airfield environment context, followed by a detection transformer-based decoder for trajectory generation.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Transformer-based encoder/decoder with a specialized PRS context sampling module and a detection transformer decoder.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Potential Reachable Set (PRS) context sampling for adaptive context collection across operational phases; detection transformer-based decoder for trajectory forecasting.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not specified in summary

paper.title: Predicting Struggling Students in CS1 Programming Using Keystroke-Level Editing Features
paper.summary: This paper investigates the feasibility of early detection of struggling students during CS1 programming exercises using keystroke-level logs. Some students fail to reach a correct solution before the exercise ends, and by the time this becomes apparent from grades or final outcomes, the opportunity for timely instructor support aimed at helping them recover may have passed. We use data from the CodeBench platform, which records real-time code editing events at the keystroke level, alongside execution and submission logs. We define two outcome groups: Breakthrough (BT) students, whose prior submissions all receive 0% and whose final submission achieves full credit, and Fully Stuck (FS) students, whose submissions all receive 0% without reaching a correct solution. To examine this feasibility, we focus on two questions: (RQ1) whether adding keystroke-level editing features improves the prediction of FS students over execution-log features alone, and (RQ2) at which stage BT and FS students can be predicted most accurately. Experiments on the 2019-1 semester of the CodeBench dataset, comprising 507 students, compare three feature configurations: execution-based features (ExecOnly), CodeMirror-based features (CMOnly), and their combination (Combined). We evaluate prediction across successive submission-based stages during each exercise. In the earliest stage, CMOnly outperforms ExecOnly (AUROC 0.654 vs. 0.575), and Combined further improves over ExecOnly by +0.098 (AUROC 0.674). Across all configurations, the earliest stage yielded the strongest predictive signal. These findings indicate that behavioral signals present at the very start of an exercise contain useful clues about whether a student will ultimately solve the problem, and that keystroke-level editing logs provide additional value for early prioritization beyond execution logs alone.
paper.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 1 table, Accepted to the 34th IEEE/ACIS International Conference on Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Networking and Parallel/Distributed Computing (SNPD 2026)

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the challenge of early detection of students who are fully stuck in CS1 programming exercises to enable timely instructor intervention before the opportunity for recovery is lost.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: This addresses the bottleneck of delayed feedback in educational AI systems, where traditional outcome-based metrics (grades/final submissions) provide signals too late for effective real-time support.
analysis.executive_summary: This work demonstrates that fine-grained behavioral signals from keystroke-level logs provide superior early predictive power for student struggle compared to coarse-grained execution logs. By identifying 'Fully Stuck' students at the earliest stages of an exercise, the approach enables proactive, data-driven prioritization of instructor support, which is critical for scalable and effective computer science education.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Improvement in AUROC for predicting Fully Stuck (FS) students using combined features over execution-only features at the earliest stage
key_metrics.baseline: Execution-based features only (ExecOnly) with AUROC 0.575

technical_breakdown.method: The study uses supervised machine learning to classify students into 'Breakthrough' (BT) and 'Fully Stuck' (FS) groups based on feature vectors derived from CodeBench logs. It compares three feature sets: execution logs, CodeMirror editing events, and a combination of both, evaluated across successive submission stages.
technical_breakdown.architecture: The pipeline involves data extraction from the CodeBench platform (keystroke and execution logs), feature engineering to create ExecOnly, CMOnly, and Combined feature sets, and classification model training/evaluation using AUROC as the primary metric.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Features are derived from real-time code editing events (CodeMirror) and execution/submission logs. The analysis focuses on the 2019-1 semester dataset with 507 students, evaluating predictive accuracy at each submission stage to determine the optimal timing for intervention.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: The paper does not specify the exact classifier algorithm (e.g., Random Forest, SVM) or computational complexity, but the feature engineering and evaluation process is standard for tabular data classification tasks, implying low computational overhead relative to deep learning approaches.

paper.title: DBcover: A White-box SQL Test Generation Framework for Coverage Improvement
paper.summary: Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMSs) are the backbone of modern data-intensive applications, making reliability and robustness critical. However, achieving high coverage in RDBMS testing remains challenging because of large codebases and complex execution logic. Traditional fuzzing relies on random SQL generation and cannot capture the correspondence between SQL inputs and internal execution paths, while symbolic execution suffers from prohibitive cost and scalability limitations.   We propose DBcover, an LLM-driven white-box SQL test generation framework based on contextual reasoning. DBcover uses lightweight dynamic analysis to extract SQL-to-path correspondence and call graphs as global context, and collects source-level information around target functions as local context. These contexts are organized in a unified knowledge graph for efficient retrieval and reuse. DBcover then performs two-phase test generation: it first selects a semantically relevant seed whose execution path is close to the uncovered target, and then guides the LLM with global and local context to generate SQL test cases that trigger previously uncovered code regions. Experiments show that DBcover achieves 80.1% and 82.3% coverage on PostgreSQL and MySQL, and is also effective on the enterprise RDBMS KingbaseES, demonstrating its practical applicability to closed-source systems.
paper.comment: Accepted to the ICSE 2026 Industry Challenge Track. 12 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables

analysis.problem_statement: Achieving high code coverage in Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMSs) is difficult due to the inability of traditional fuzzing to link SQL inputs to internal execution paths and the scalability limitations of symbolic execution.

analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the critical reliability gap in data-intensive infrastructure by leveraging LLMs for white-box test generation. It bridges the semantic gap between high-level SQL queries and low-level code execution paths, enabling targeted coverage improvement in both open-source and closed-source enterprise databases.

paper.title: Resilient Decentralized Wireless Federated Learning via Gradient Tracking with AdamW
paper.summary: Wireless Internet-of-Things (IoT) edge networks require decentralized learning (DecL) methods that can operate reliably under both heterogeneous local data and communication-constrained wireless links. However, existing decentralized optimization schemes often incur substantial communication overhead and degraded performance when transmissions are constrained by strict airtime budgets, fading channels, and packet losses. This paper proposes QEF-GT-AdamW, a communication-efficient and outage-resilient algorithm for DecL over wireless communication (WCom) networks. The proposed method combines gradient tracking to mitigate the effect of non-IID data, AdamW-based adaptive optimization to improve training stability, and dual-stream biased quantization with error feedback to reduce communication payloads for both model and tracking exchanges. To address unreliable broadcast communication, the proposed framework further employs a local fallback strategy when scheduled packets are not successfully received. We explicitly model the effect of bandwidth, transmit power, airtime constraints, and fading channels on DecL performance, and establish convergence guarantees for the proposed algorithm under compressed and unreliable wireless communication. Experimental results on heterogeneous MNIST and CIFAR-10 settings show that QEF-GT-AdamW consistently improves robustness and convergence performance over representative DecL baselines while achieving favorable accuracy-communication trade-offs under limited wireless resources.

analysis.executive_summary: This work is significant for the edge AI landscape as it provides a robust framework for federated learning in resource-constrained IoT environments where traditional methods fail due to communication unreliability. By integrating gradient tracking with adaptive optimization and quantization, it enables practical deployment of decentralized models in real-world wireless networks with high packet loss and non-IID data.

paper.title: Joint Beamforming Design and Port Selection in Fluid Antenna-Assisted Multi-Cell Networks: A Personalized Federated Learning Approach
paper.summary: This paper investigates joint beamforming and port selection in multi-cell fluid antenna-assisted (FAS) networks. In such networks, active beamforming and discrete FA port selection are coupled through intra-cell and inter-cell interference and are jointly optimized to maximize the weighted sum-rate (WSR). We develop a federated representation learning (FedRep) framework with a position-aware dual-branch deep neural network (PA-DNN). The PA-DNN uses channel state information and port positional encoding as inputs, and jointly outputs beamforming vectors and port selections through two task-specific branches. To support decentralized training across heterogeneous cells, the FedRep framework shares global beamforming-related parameters among base stations while keeping port-selection parameters local for cell-specific adaptation. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme achieves a higher weighted sum-rate than conventional FL and port-selection benchmark schemes.

analysis.executive_summary: This work is significant for the evolution of 6G networks by integrating fluid antenna systems with federated learning, allowing for adaptive, location-aware resource allocation without compromising user or network privacy. It demonstrates that personalized federated learning can outperform conventional methods in complex, interference-heavy multi-cell environments.

paper.title: Reconstructing Humans and Objects in Interaction using Large Reconstruction Models
paper.summary: Estimation of Human-Object Interactions in 3D (3D HOI) is a fundamental problem in 3D computer vision with applications in AR/VR, robotics, and embodied AI. However, reconstructing these interactions in 3D remains challenging due to depth ambiguities, occlusions, and object shape variability. Existing approaches are primarily concerned with reprojection and contact constraints, fitting parametric human models and object templates to 2D images. In this paper, we explore a different avenue. We present MILO, a framework that leverages the visual capabilities of Large Reconstruction Models (LRMs) to recover detailed 3D human-object interactions from a single image. Our key observation is that LRMs provide a powerful geometric scaffold that preserves relative human-object arrangement and proximity cues. This significantly simplifies the reconstruction procedure, reframing the problem as interpreting the LRM mesh: we segment it into human and object components, fit a parametric body model to the human part, and optionally align an object template to the object part (if such a template is available). MILO achieves strong reconstruction accuracy and outperforms existing baselines across multiple benchmarks and interaction scenarios. Our code is available at https://ac5113.github.io/MILO.

By reframing the problem as interpreting an LRM mesh rather than fitting parametric models directly to 2D images, it simplifies the reconstruction process and improves accuracy in handling occlusions and relative positioning.

paper.title: CODE: Cross-Modal Calibration and Dynamic Suppression for Open World Object Detection
paper.summary: Open World Object Detection (OWOD) built on multimodal foundation models often suffers from semantic ambiguity caused by unidirectional text-to-vision matching, while rigid outlier penalties may over-suppress unknown objects near known-class decision boundaries. We propose CODE (Cross-Modal Calibration and Dynamic Suppression), a unified inference-time framework with three complementary components. Cross-Modal Joint Confidence Calibration injects global visual prototypes to calibrate text-driven known-class predictions. Uncertainty-Guided Universal Objectness Enhancement measures classification hesitation from local visual responses to strengthen potential unknown objects. Dynamic Outlier Suppression via Confidence Margin replaces rigid suppression with a margin-aware adjustment that preserves ambiguous out-of-distribution instances. Experiments on the Real-World Detection benchmark demonstrate that, with the OWL-ViT L/14 backbone, CODE achieves 21.7 U-mAP and 40.8 K-mAP in Task 1, surpassing the previous state of the art by 2.6 and 2.3 points, respectively.

analysis.problem_statement: Open World Object Detection models based on multimodal foundation models suffer from semantic ambiguity due to unidirectional text-to-vision matching and the over-suppression of unknown objects near known-class decision boundaries caused by rigid outlier penalties.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Semantic ambiguity in cross-modal alignment and the trade-off between suppressing false positives (known classes) and preserving true positives (unknown classes) in open-world scenarios.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses a critical limitation in open-world object detection where rigid outlier suppression mechanisms inadvertently discard ambiguous unknown objects that are semantically close to known classes. By introducing an inference-time calibration framework, it enhances the robustness of multimodal foundation models without requiring retraining, thereby improving the detection of out-of-distribution instances in real-world environments.

key_metrics.primary_metric: U-mAP and K-mAP on the Real-World Detection benchmark (Task 1)
key_metrics.baseline: Previous state-of-the-art methods using OWL-ViT L/14 backbone

technical_breakdown.method: CODE is a unified inference-time framework that combines cross-modal confidence calibration, uncertainty-guided objectness enhancement, and dynamic outlier suppression to refine predictions from multimodal foundation models.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Three complementary components: 1) Cross-Modal Joint Confidence Calibration, 2) Uncertainty-Guided Universal Objectness Enhancement, 3) Dynamic Outlier Suppression via Confidence Margin.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Injects global visual prototypes to calibrate text-driven predictions; measures classification hesitation from local visual responses to boost unknown object scores; replaces rigid penalties with margin-aware adjustments to preserve ambiguous OOD instances.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Inference-time framework, implying no additional training cost but added computational overhead during the prediction phase for calibration and suppression logic.

paper.title: TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attacks against Image-to-Video Generation Models
paper.summary: In recent years, image-to-video (I2V) generation models have made remarkable progress in subject consistency and temporal coherence, enabling high quality video synthesis. However, these advances also introduce new safety risks. Existing studies mainly focus on jailbreak attacks involving single frame violations, while largely overlooking the temporal dimension unique to video generation models. In this paper, we investigate three attack scenarios and uncover a temporal vulnerability in I2V systems: unsafe semantics may emerge not from a single frame, but from semantic composition over time. We further identify two key challenges in such attacks: temporal abstraction and semantic camouflage. To address these issues, we propose TempJail, a novel temporal jailbreak framework for I2V systems. For temporal abstraction, we decompose a target malicious caption into an initial frame visual condition and a temporal text instruction. For semantic camouflage, on the image side we model semantic injection as controlled latent perturbation in diffusion sampling and introduce gradient guidance from pretrained encoders. On the text side, we rewrite the caption into an innocuous ``subject-action-scene'' template that bypasses safety filters while preserving temporal guidance. In the black-box inference phase, these two modalities jointly enable malicious semantics to be gradually triggered over time. Experiments on closed-source commercial models, including Kling, Seedance, Veo and PixVerse, show that TempJail improves attack success rate over prior state-of-the-art methods by 23.3\% under GPT-5.2 evaluation and 22.0\% under human evaluation. Our codes are available at \href{https://github.com/luqi-glory/TempJail}{GitHub}.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the lack of safety in image-to-video (I2V) generation models, specifically targeting the temporal vulnerability where unsafe semantics emerge from the composition of frames over time rather than from single-frame violations.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Safety and alignment in multimodal generative models, specifically the gap in temporal safety filtering for video synthesis.
analysis.executive_summary: This research highlights a critical blind spot in current AI safety protocols: the assumption that video safety can be ensured by checking individual frames ignores the semantic risks introduced by temporal coherence. By demonstrating that malicious content can be constructed through the gradual evolution of benign frames and text, the paper exposes a significant security flaw in state-of-the-art commercial video generators. It provides a framework to understand and test these temporal jailbreaks, urging the development of more robust, time-aware safety mechanisms.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Attack Success Rate (ASR)
key_metrics.baseline: Prior state-of-the-art jailbreak methods

technical_breakdown.method: The proposed TempJail framework decomposes malicious intent into an initial visual condition and a temporal text instruction to exploit the temporal dimension of I2V models. It combines latent space perturbation for image generation with semantic camouflage in text to bypass safety filters while triggering unsafe semantics over time.
technical_breakdown.architecture: A two-modality attack pipeline consisting of an image-side component (controlled latent perturbation in diffusion sampling) and a text-side component (rewriting captions into innocuous 'subject-action-scene' templates).
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses gradient guidance from pretrained encoders for semantic injection in the image modality. Employs a 'subject-action-scene' template for text rewriting to maintain temporal guidance while appearing benign to safety filters. Evaluated on closed-source models including Kling, Seedance, Veo, and PixVerse.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not specified in the abstract; requires access to diffusion model internals for latent perturbation and gradient computation, implying high computational cost for attack generation.

paper.title: From Reasoning to Pixels: Grounded Medical Multimodal LLMs for VQA and Segmentation
paper.summary: Although Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated impressive performance in Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA), their reliance on global image features often lacks precise pixel-level grounding, thereby limiting clinical trustworthiness. To bridge the semantic gap between high-level clinical reasoning and spatial localization, we propose \textsc{\textsc{MedREAL}} (\textbf{Med}ical \textbf{RE}asoning-driven \textbf{A}nswering and \textbf{L}ocalization), a unified framework that seamlessly aligns linguistic reasoning with spatial grounding. Specifically, \textsc{MedREAL} introduces \textbf{S}eg \textbf{A}nchored \textbf{R}easoning \textbf{P}ooling (SARP) to distill task-relevant semantic evidence directly from \texttt{[SEG]} tokens within the MLLM's hidden states. Furthermore, a \textbf{R}easoning-to-\textbf{V}isual (R2V) fusion mechanism is proposed to effectively inject these reasoning-aware features into a segmentation pipeline for accurate mask decoding. To facilitate this paradigm, we construct MedRAVS-13K, a comprehensive dataset comprising 13,824 expertly validated samples across four diverse imaging modalities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that \textsc{MedREAL} significantly outperforms state-of-the-arts, achieving 68.49\% gIoU and 70.47\% cIoU on benchmark evaluations. By generating evidence masks that are strictly consistent with textual diagnoses, \textsc{MedREAL} provides a robust, interpretable framework for reasoning-driven medical image analysis.

analysis.problem_statement: Medical Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) lack precise pixel-level grounding, leading to a disconnect between high-level clinical reasoning and spatial localization which limits clinical trustworthiness.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Lack of spatial grounding and interpretability in medical MLLMs, specifically the semantic gap between textual reasoning and pixel-level segmentation.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the critical need for interpretable AI in healthcare by aligning linguistic reasoning with spatial localization. By introducing a unified framework that generates evidence masks consistent with textual diagnoses, it enhances the clinical utility and trustworthiness of medical image analysis tools.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Generalized Intersection over Union (gIoU) and Class Intersection over Union (cIoU) on benchmark evaluations
key_metrics.baseline: State-of-the-art methods (specific baselines not named in abstract)

technical_breakdown.method: A unified framework, MedREAL, that aligns linguistic reasoning with spatial grounding by distilling semantic evidence from MLLM hidden states and injecting it into a segmentation pipeline.
technical_breakdown.architecture: MedREAL framework comprising Seg Anchored Reasoning Pooling (SARP) and a Reasoning-to-Visual (R2V) fusion mechanism.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: SARP distills task-relevant semantic evidence from [SEG] tokens in MLLM hidden states; R2V fuses these reasoning-aware features into a segmentation pipeline for mask decoding. Evaluated on MedRAVS-13K, a dataset of 13,824 validated samples across four imaging modalities.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not specified in abstract; involves MLLM hidden state extraction and fusion with a segmentation decoder.

paper.title: MedFG-VQA: Low-Frequency Memory and Graph Attention for Lightweight Medical VQA
paper.summary: Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA) holds significant promise for clinical decision support, yet faces challenges due to limited annotated data and the high computational demands of existing large vision-language models. We propose MedFG-VQA, a lightweight framework that leverages a memory bank to augment DCT-based low-frequency features and employs graph-enhanced cross-attention for effective visual-textual alignment. Specifically, our approach features two key components: Frequency-Memory Fusion (FMF), which enhances low-frequency features by retrieving from a learnable memory bank built on DCT decomposition, and Graph-Aware Cross-Attention (GACA), which aligns visual-textual features via cross-attention and refines them through graph-convolutional aggregation. To address data scarcity, we construct SynMed-VQA, a large-scale synthetic dataset comprising over 2 million question-answer pairs across 9 imaging modalities and 10 major organs, generated with GPT-4o. Extensive experiments on SynMed-VQA and three other standard biomedical VQA benchmarks demonstrate that MedFG-VQA achieves competitive or superior performance compared to much larger models while maintaining significantly lower computational costs, highlighting its efficiency and potential for clinical deployment.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the high computational cost and data scarcity challenges in Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA) by proposing a lightweight framework that enhances feature alignment without relying on large vision-language models.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Computational efficiency and data scarcity in medical multimodal learning.
analysis.executive_summary: This work is significant because it decouples high-performance medical VQA from the need for massive, computationally expensive vision-language models, enabling more efficient clinical deployment. By introducing a synthetic dataset (SynMed-VQA) and a frequency-memory fusion architecture, it provides a scalable solution to the limited annotated data problem in biomedical imaging.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Competitive or superior performance compared to much larger models with significantly lower computational costs.
key_metrics.baseline: Much larger existing large vision-language models

technical_breakdown.method: The framework utilizes a memory bank to augment DCT-based low-frequency features and employs graph-enhanced cross-attention for visual-textual alignment.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Two key components: Frequency-Memory Fusion (FMF) for enhancing low-frequency features via learnable memory retrieval, and Graph-Aware Cross-Attention (GACA) for aligning and refining features via cross-attention and graph-convolutional aggregation.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses DCT decomposition for feature extraction, a learnable memory bank, and graph-convolutional aggregation. The synthetic dataset SynMed-VQA contains over 2 million QA pairs across 9 imaging modalities and 10 organs, generated using GPT-4o.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Lightweight framework designed for significantly lower computational costs compared to large vision-language models.

paper.title: LLaVAFlow: Preserving Latent Alignment Flow for Parameter-Efficient Multimodal Fine-Tuning
paper.summary: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) exhibit strong generalization, visual instruction tuning for downstream tasks inevitably causes catastrophic forgetting, impairing overall generalization. While existing methods regulate weight updates to reduce forgetting, they overlook the fundamental cross-modal alignment in MLLMs. Based on prior work and our observations, we argue that cross-modal alignment is implicitly captured in the information-compression trajectory. To preserve the alignment flow embedded in the trajectory, we propose LLaVAFlow, an information-theoretic distillation framework. First, we compress the mutual information between the extracted relations and MLLM embeddings, encouraging a learnable module to produce a refined alignment flow that benefits downstream tasks. Second, we maximize the mutual information between the extracted alignment flows of the pretrained and fine-tuned MLLMs, enabling the transfer of compact alignment information. Extensive experiments show that LLaVAFlow is an effective plug-and-play framework that preserves alignment flow and enhances both downstream performance and generalization.

analysis.problem_statement: Visual instruction tuning of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) causes catastrophic forgetting that impairs generalization by disrupting the fundamental cross-modal alignment.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Catastrophic forgetting and loss of cross-modal alignment during fine-tuning.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the trade-off between task-specific performance and generalization in MLLMs by preserving the 'alignment flow' during fine-tuning. It proposes an information-theoretic distillation framework that transfers compact alignment information from pretrained models to fine-tuned ones, enhancing both downstream task performance and overall generalization capabilities.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Preservation of alignment flow and enhancement of downstream performance and generalization
key_metrics.baseline: Existing methods that regulate weight updates to reduce forgetting

technical_breakdown.method: LLaVAFlow is an information-theoretic distillation framework that compresses mutual information between extracted relations and MLLM embeddings to produce a refined alignment flow, then maximizes mutual information between pretrained and fine-tuned alignment flows.
technical_breakdown.architecture: A plug-and-play framework incorporating a learnable module that generates refined alignment flows, integrated into the MLLM fine-tuning pipeline.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses mutual information compression and maximization techniques to transfer compact alignment information from pretrained to fine-tuned models.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not specified in abstract; likely adds minimal overhead as it is described as a plug-and-play framework.

paper.title: Glass Surface Detection Grounded in 3D Visual Geometry
paper.summary: Glass surface detection (GSD) is critical for scene understanding and reconstruction, and yet remains challenging due to the transparency and reflectivity of glass surfaces. Existing GSD methods typically rely on 2D appearance cues, which may fail in geometrically ambiguous scenes. In this paper, we propose a paradigm shift: grounding GSD in 3D visual geometry to explicitly model the physical existence of glass surfaces. Our method first distills rich 3D priors from the visual geometry grounded transformer (VGGT) and generates glass-aware 3D representations. It then exploits multi-tasking learning with a novel glass detection head, consisting of two core modules: a Frequency Self-Attention Module (FSAM) that identifies glass-specific spectral features for glass surface localization, and a Geometry Grounding Block (GeGB) that selectively grounds 2D features in 3D geometry for glass surface segmentation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance across seven standard GSD benchmarks, generalizes well to video/multi-modal data, and substantially improves reconstruction in glass scenes. Code is available in https://github.com/YT3DVision/VGGT_GLASS.
paper.comment: 9 pages, 10 figures. Accepted by ACM Multimedia 2026

analysis.problem_statement: Existing glass surface detection methods fail in geometrically ambiguous scenes because they rely solely on 2D appearance cues, ignoring the physical 3D geometry of transparent and reflective surfaces.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Lack of 3D geometric grounding in 2D-based semantic segmentation for transparent materials.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses a critical gap in scene understanding by shifting glass detection from 2D appearance-based heuristics to a 3D geometry-grounded paradigm. By leveraging 3D priors from VGGT, it enables robust detection of transparent surfaces that are otherwise invisible or ambiguous in 2D projections, which is essential for accurate reconstruction in complex real-world environments.

key_metrics.primary_metric: State-of-the-art performance on standard Glass Surface Detection (GSD) benchmarks
key_metrics.baseline: Existing 2D appearance-based GSD methods

technical_breakdown.method: The method distills 3D priors from the Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT) to generate glass-aware 3D representations, then uses multi-task learning with a specialized detection head to segment glass surfaces.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Key components include the Frequency Self-Attention Module (FSAM) for spectral feature identification and the Geometry Grounding Block (GeGB) for grounding 2D features in 3D geometry.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Utilizes VGGT for 3D prior distillation, FSAM for identifying glass-specific spectral features, and GeGB for selective 2D-to-3D feature grounding.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not specified in abstract; relies on transformer-based 3D prior distillation and multi-task learning heads.

paper.title: Beyond Atomic Layouts: Compositional Design Understanding with Vision-Language Models
paper.summary: Layout understanding, or the interpretation of element organization, is essential for document analysis, user interface (UI) creation, and graphic design. While recent vision-language models (VLMs) excel at interpreting atomic layouts composed of independent elements, they struggle with compositional layouts that require reasoning over visually entangled elements within hierarchical multi-layer structures. In this paper, we introduce a new task, compositional layout understanding, and present CoDeLayout, a VQA dataset of ~20K real-world multi-layer layouts annotated with compositional element pairs and design intent. Through empirical analysis on CoDeLayout, we identify two key challenges for existing VLMs: semantic drift between textual metadata and visual content, and structural ambiguity in hierarchical inter-element relationships. To address these challenges, we propose MASON, a post-training paradigm that integrates multimodal alignment (MA) and structural perception (SP). MA enhances element interpretation by grounding metadata-defined elements to their visual counterparts, mitigating semantic drift, while SP models layer-aware inter-element spatial relationships to improve hierarchical understanding and reduce structural ambiguity. Experiments reveal substantial gaps in existing VLMs: even the strongest baseline, GPT-o3, achieves only 79.68% accuracy, whereas Qwen2.5-VL 7B with MASON reaches 91.66%. Notably, MASON surpasses full-data Direct Finetune using only 30% of the training data and scales better with additional data.

analysis.problem_statement: Existing vision-language models fail to accurately interpret compositional layouts involving hierarchical multi-layer structures and visually entangled elements, suffering from semantic drift and structural ambiguity.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Limitations in hierarchical spatial reasoning and multimodal alignment for complex, non-atomic visual structures.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses a critical gap in document and UI analysis by introducing a new task for compositional layout understanding. It demonstrates that current state-of-the-art VLMs struggle with hierarchical relationships, proposing a post-training paradigm that significantly outperforms larger models using less data.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Accuracy on the CoDeLayout VQA dataset
key_metrics.baseline: GPT-o3 (79.68%) and Qwen2.5-VL 7B without MASON

technical_breakdown.method: MASON, a post-training paradigm integrating Multimodal Alignment (MA) and Structural Perception (SP) to ground metadata to visual elements and model layer-aware spatial relationships.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Built upon Qwen2.5-VL 7B, incorporating specific modules for metadata-to-visual grounding and hierarchical inter-element relationship modeling.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses a VQA dataset (CoDeLayout) of ~20K real-world layouts; MA mitigates semantic drift by aligning textual metadata with visual counterparts; SP reduces structural ambiguity by modeling layer-aware spatial interactions.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Achieves superior performance using only 30% of the training data required for full-data Direct Finetuning, indicating higher data efficiency and better scaling properties.

paper.title: FLARE: A Failure-Aware Framework for Autonomous Correction and Recovery in Visual-Language Robotic Manipulation
paper.summary: Vision-Language-Action Models~(VLAs) have demonstrated significant promise in generalizing to complex, long-horizon robotic manipulation tasks. However, their performance remains brittle, as they are typically trained on trajectory-monotonic, failure-free demonstrations. This reliance on ``perfect" data leaves them unable to recover from common execution errors, such as a missed grasp, a dropped object, or an unexpected collision. In this paper, we propose FLARE, a novel framework that endows VLAs with robust error recovery capabilities through a ``Retry" and ``Reset" paradigm. First, we introduce a ``Retry" mechanism by injecting perturbation and bridging segments that decouple robot pose from environment state into demonstrations, enabling the policy to autonomously handle execution deviations. Second, to address critical, state-breaking (OOD) failures, we introduce a ``Reset" pipeline. We leverage an MLLM for offline failure analysis to automatically identify OOD states from execution videos. This analysis enables the efficient, targeted collection of a small library of object-centric ``Reset" skills, which are trained to restore the environment to a task-valid state. Our full framework integrates these learned policies. At inference, an online MLLM monitor arbitrates between task execution and ``Reset" skills. Experiments on challenging, contact-rich manipulation tasks show our approach significantly improves task success and robustness.

analysis.problem_statement: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are brittle in long-horizon robotic manipulation because they are trained on failure-free demonstrations and lack the capability to recover from execution errors such as missed grasps or collisions.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Lack of robustness and error recovery capabilities in VLA models due to reliance on trajectory-monotonic, failure-free training data.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses a critical limitation in general-purpose robotic manipulation by enabling VLAs to handle real-world execution deviations. By introducing a framework that combines autonomous retry mechanisms with MLLM-guided reset skills, it significantly enhances the robustness of robotic agents in contact-rich environments.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Task success rate and robustness in challenging, contact-rich manipulation tasks
key_metrics.baseline: Standard VLA models trained on failure-free demonstrations

technical_breakdown.method: The FLARE framework employs a 'Retry' and 'Reset' paradigm. 'Retry' involves injecting perturbation and bridging segments into demonstrations to decouple robot pose from environment state, allowing the policy to handle deviations. 'Reset' uses an MLLM for offline failure analysis to identify Out-of-Distribution (OOD) states and train a library of object-centric skills to restore task-valid states.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Integrates a VLA policy with an online MLLM monitor that arbitrates between task execution and the execution of learned 'Reset' skills.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses MLLMs for offline failure analysis from execution videos to identify OOD states. Trains a small library of object-centric 'Reset' skills. Injects perturbation and bridging segments into training data for the 'Retry' mechanism.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Requires offline MLLM analysis and targeted data collection for reset skills, in addition to standard VLA training. Inference involves an online MLLM monitor for arbitration.

paper.title: NeuDonatello: Uncertainty-Aware Framework for Accurate Neural SDF Learning
paper.summary: Neural surface reconstruction has emerged as a powerful paradigm for recovering high-quality 3D surfaces from multi-view images. However, recovering accurate geometry solely from RGB images remains challenging due to uncertainties arising from textureless regions, occlusions, and inherent scene ambiguities. Existing methods often overlook such uncertainties, leading to inaccurate estimates of the signed distance function (SDF). We introduce NeuDonatello, a novel framework that models and leverages SDF uncertainty to improve surface reconstruction. Central to our approach is to model spatially varying uncertainty using a Monte Carlo sampling strategy. Using this uncertainty, we develop an adaptive regularization that selectively strengthens geometric constraints where RGB supervision is unreliable, avoiding incorrect surface reconstruction. We further introduce an uncertainty-aware scale parameter for the SDF-to-density conversion. Conditioned on uncertainty, this design enables more accurate modeling of spatially varying densities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that NeuDonatello achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction accuracy, with robust performance across diverse scenes using only posed RGB images.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the challenge of recovering accurate 3D surfaces from multi-view RGB images where geometric ambiguities, textureless regions, and occlusions lead to unreliable Signed Distance Function (SDF) estimates in existing neural reconstruction methods.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Geometric ambiguity and lack of robustness in implicit surface reconstruction due to insufficient or noisy RGB supervision in textureless or occluded regions.
analysis.executive_summary: NeuDonatello improves the reliability of neural surface reconstruction by explicitly modeling spatially varying uncertainty in the SDF, allowing the system to distinguish between reliable and unreliable geometric cues. This approach prevents the propagation of errors from ambiguous image regions into the final 3D mesh, enhancing robustness for real-world applications where perfect texture or visibility is not guaranteed.

key_metrics.primary_metric: State-of-the-art reconstruction accuracy
key_metrics.baseline: Existing neural surface reconstruction methods

technical_breakdown.method: The framework models SDF uncertainty using Monte Carlo sampling to identify regions where RGB supervision is unreliable. It applies adaptive regularization to strengthen geometric constraints in these high-uncertainty areas and uses an uncertainty-aware scale parameter for SDF-to-density conversion to model spatially varying densities more accurately.
technical_breakdown.architecture: A neural SDF learning framework incorporating a Monte Carlo sampling module for uncertainty estimation, an adaptive regularization mechanism, and a modified SDF-to-density conversion layer conditioned on uncertainty.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Monte Carlo sampling strategy for spatially varying uncertainty; adaptive regularization that selectively strengthens constraints based on uncertainty levels; uncertainty-conditioned scale parameter for density modeling.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Likely increased computational overhead due to Monte Carlo sampling during training, though specific training times or FLOPs are not provided in the metadata.

paper.title: Empowering Compact LLMs with Fusion of Layer-wise Exits for Recommendation
paper.summary: Large language model-based recommender systems (LLM-RSs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities, but are computationally unsustainable for many real-world applications. Compact LLMs offer a practical alternative, yet their reduced capacity often requires reasoning or knowledge distillation methods that increase latency or depend on larger models. Combined with autoregressive generation, these approaches face severe scalability bottlenecks. In contrast, discriminative LLM-RSs enable efficient full-corpus ranking through embedding similarity, but compact backbones remain limited in expressiveness and structural adaptivity. We propose the Fusion of Layer-wise Exits for Sequential Recommendation (FLEXRec), a discriminative framework that enhances compact LLMs while retaining scalable full-corpus ranking. FLEXRec inserts prediction heads (i.e., exits) at multiple transformer layers and adaptively fuses their score distributions. An adaptive continuous router (AC-Router) dynamically selects both the number and identity of exits for each user sequence, while a novel target-k hinge loss regulates routing sparsity. Experiments on three real-world datasets with Qwen 3 1.7B and Llama 3.2 3B show that FLEXRec achieves state-of-the-art accuracy among competing methods while remaining highly efficient. Code: https://github.com/xurong-liang/FLEXRec

analysis.problem_statement: Compact Large Language Models (LLMs) used for recommendation systems suffer from limited expressiveness and structural adaptivity when used in discriminative frameworks for efficient full-corpus ranking.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Computational sustainability and scalability of LLM-based recommender systems, specifically balancing the accuracy of compact models with the efficiency of discriminative ranking.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the trade-off between the high accuracy of large LLMs and the computational efficiency required for real-world recommendation systems. By introducing a discriminative framework that fuses predictions from multiple transformer layers, it enables compact LLMs to achieve state-of-the-art performance without the latency penalties associated with autoregressive generation or knowledge distillation.

key_metrics.primary_metric: State-of-the-art accuracy among competing methods while maintaining high efficiency
key_metrics.baseline: Competing methods using Qwen 3 1.7B and Llama 3.2 3B

technical_breakdown.method: FLEXRec inserts prediction heads at multiple transformer layers and adaptively fuses their score distributions using an adaptive continuous router that dynamically selects the number and identity of exits for each user sequence.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Discriminative framework with multi-layer prediction heads (exits) and an Adaptive Continuous Router (AC-Router).
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses a target-k hinge loss to regulate routing sparsity and enables efficient full-corpus ranking through embedding similarity.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Highly efficient, retaining scalable full-corpus ranking capabilities compared to autoregressive or distillation-based approaches.

paper.title: Topology-Masked Unified Backbone for Joint Feature Interaction and Multi-Domain Sequence Modeling
paper.summary: Large-scale post-click conversion rate (CVR) prediction requires jointly modeling heterogeneous feature interactions and dependencies over multi-domain user behavior sequences. Existing industrial ranking models usually handle these two aspects with separate modules. Recent unified architectures attempt to incorporate them into a single framework, but such unification often relies on coordination between modules and does not fully organize all information sources within the same interaction space. To address this problem, we propose MaskRec, a topology-masked unified token interaction architecture for feature interaction and multi-domain sequence modeling. MaskRec transforms heterogeneous features, multi-domain behavior sequences, and contextual signals into unified token representations, and further introduces learnable global memory tokens and domain-level memory tokens as information aggregation nodes. Based on this unified token space, MaskRec designs a structured attention mask, TopoMask, which selectively enables or blocks attention connections according to the structural differences and modeling requirements of different information sources. In this way, heterogeneous feature interaction and multi-domain sequence modeling are performed within the same topology-constrained attention process. In addition, MaskRec incorporates a dual-path interactive query generation module to inject candidate-conditioned user--item interaction signals before the unified backbone. Experiments on the Tencent Advertising Algorithm Competition dataset show that MaskRec achieves stable improvements over the official baseline, validating the effectiveness of the proposed unified framework for industrial CVR prediction.
paper.comment: Accepted to the TAAC-KDD Cup 2026 Workshop. Recipient of the Unified Block Innovation Award

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the challenge of jointly modeling heterogeneous feature interactions and multi-domain user behavior sequences within a single, unified interaction space for large-scale post-click conversion rate (CVR) prediction.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Modular fragmentation in industrial ranking models, where separate modules for feature interaction and sequence modeling fail to fully organize all information sources within the same interaction space, limiting the capture of cross-domain dependencies.
analysis.executive_summary: MaskRec proposes a topology-masked unified token architecture that integrates heterogeneous features and multi-domain sequences into a single attention-based framework. By using structured attention masks to manage different information sources, it enables more coherent joint modeling for industrial CVR prediction, offering a potential paradigm shift from modular to unified backbones in recommendation systems.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Stable improvements over the official baseline in CVR prediction
key_metrics.baseline: Official baseline of the Tencent Advertising Algorithm Competition (TAAC-KDD Cup 2026)

technical_breakdown.method: The solution transforms heterogeneous features, multi-domain behavior sequences, and contextual signals into unified token representations. It introduces learnable global and domain-level memory tokens as aggregation nodes and applies a structured attention mask (TopoMask) to selectively enable or block attention connections based on structural differences and modeling requirements.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Key components include a unified token interaction backbone, learnable global memory tokens, domain-level memory tokens, a TopoMask structured attention mechanism, and a dual-path interactive query generation module for injecting candidate-conditioned user-item interaction signals.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Specific techniques include the design of TopoMask to constrain attention topology, the use of memory tokens for information aggregation, and the integration of candidate-conditioned signals via a dual-path query generation module before the main backbone.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not explicitly stated, but the use of a unified attention mechanism with structured masks and multiple token types suggests higher computational overhead compared to simple modular approaches, though potentially more efficient than fully dense cross-attention over all heterogeneous sources.

paper.title: Risks and Controls for Multi-Agent Systems: an analytical framework for deployment of AI agents across organisational boundaries
paper.summary: This report presents a framework to help organisations, policymakers and researchers reason about the risks that emerge when AI agents interact with each other, how those risks change as interactions cross organisational boundaries, and the controls that may help address them.   As organisations deploy AI agents, those agents will increasingly interact with each other: inside the organisation, with the agents of partners, customers and suppliers, and with unknown counterparties on the open internet. Failures can emerge from the interactions themselves, and once those interactions cross an organisation's perimeter, no single organisation can fully see, control or govern them.   The report introduces three deployment tiers, defined by the minimum common governance binding any two interacting agents: singular governance, where one organisation governs every agent; federated governance, where multiple organisations deploy into a shared environment under agreed rules; and open environments, where agents operate with no central authority and shared standards are adopted voluntarily if at all.   Within each tier, the report examines risk factors, failure modes and available controls. It identifies who is positioned to apply the controls, and where no actor is positioned to act, it characterises the gap and the collective action required to close it.

analysis.executive_summary: As AI agents increasingly interact across organizational perimeters, traditional single-organization governance models fail to account for emergent risks and control gaps. This framework provides a tiered approach to categorize these interactions and identify specific failure modes and necessary controls, highlighting areas where collective action is required to close governance voids.

paper.title: Not All Eval-Awareness Is Equal: Capabilities Framing Predicts Compliance
paper.summary: Steering interventions targeting eval-awareness, a model's recognition that it is being tested, are increasingly used in safety evaluation pipelines, where evaluation-awareness is treated as a single quantity to be suppressed. We show that verbalized eval-awareness in chain-of-thought can be identified as capabilities-flavored ("the user is testing my ability to follow instructions"), safety-flavored ("the user is testing my boundaries"), both, or neither: framings that predict compliance very differently. On Qwen3-32B over the FORTRESS dataset, capabilities-framing predicts compliance with a +24 to +46 percentage-point gap over safety-framing across all tested steering conditions. A CoT-prefill intervention on eval-awareness-negative rollouts suggests the link is causal, with 10 of 11 prefills shifting compliance in the predicted direction. Then, eval-awareness is not behaviorally uniform: aggregate suppression rates can move while the safety-relevant component does not, and the same "X% suppression of eval-awareness" can correspond to qualitatively different behavioral outcomes.
paper.comment: 5 pages (14 appendices), 5 figures, presented at 2026 ICML Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the limitation of treating evaluation-awareness as a uniform scalar quantity in safety steering, demonstrating that different verbalized framings of eval-awareness lead to divergent compliance behaviors.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Safety evaluation reliability and the behavioral unpredictability of steering interventions targeting model self-awareness.
analysis.executive_summary: This work reveals that aggregate suppression of evaluation-awareness is insufficient for safety assurance because it masks critical distinctions between capabilities-focused and safety-focused self-perceptions. By identifying that capabilities-framing significantly predicts higher compliance than safety-framing, the paper highlights a causal mechanism where specific internal narratives drive behavioral outcomes, necessitating more granular steering strategies in AI safety pipelines.

key_metrics.baseline: Safety-framed eval-awareness compliance rates

technical_breakdown.method: The study analyzes chain-of-thought (CoT) outputs to classify eval-awareness into capabilities-flavored, safety-flavored, both, or neither categories, then correlates these framings with compliance on the FORTRESS dataset. It further employs CoT-prefill interventions on eval-awareness-negative rollouts to establish causal links between framing and compliance direction.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Utilizes Qwen3-32B as the base model, evaluated against the FORTRESS dataset. The analysis focuses on the internal CoT representations rather than modifying the model's weights, relying on prefilling techniques for intervention.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Key techniques include semantic classification of CoT tokens for eval-awareness framing, statistical analysis of compliance gaps across steering conditions, and causal inference via CoT-prefill (10/11 successful directional shifts).
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Inference-time complexity is dominated by the generation of CoT rollouts and prefilling; no additional training or fine-tuning is required, making it computationally efficient relative to weight-based steering methods.

paper.title: MM-Spectrum: Multimodal Multi-spectral Molecular Structural Elucidation with a Stable MoE Framework
paper.summary: Inferring molecular structures from multimodal spectroscopic measurements requires integrating complementary yet highly heterogeneous signals. However, the common paradigm of directly concatenating multispectral sequences can exhibit anomalous performance degradation, primarily due to pronounced heterogeneity and the resulting multimodal imbalance across modalities. As a remedy, we propose MM-Spectrum, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts framework tailored for multimodal multispectral spectra-to-structure elucidation. To better match the information characteristics under multispectral imbalance, MM-Spectrum introduces an explicit modality-aware routing mechanism that exposes spectral identity to the router in addition to token content representations. Moreover, it incorporates shared and interaction experts, together with heterogeneous expert capacities, to extract multispectral modality-unique and cross-modal synergistic information while suppressing noise-induced interference. Across full-modality, bimodal, and missing-modality settings on molecular structural elucidation, MM-Spectrum achieves consistent and substantial improvements, supported by ablation studies and interpretability analyses.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the performance degradation and multimodal imbalance issues that arise when directly concatenating heterogeneous multispectral signals for molecular structural elucidation.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Multimodal integration and heterogeneity handling in sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing.
analysis.executive_summary: This work introduces a modality-aware routing mechanism within a sparse MoE framework to effectively integrate complementary yet heterogeneous spectroscopic data. By explicitly exposing spectral identity to the router and using heterogeneous expert capacities, it mitigates noise-induced interference and multimodal imbalance, offering a robust solution for complex scientific data fusion.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Consistent and substantial improvements in molecular structural elucidation accuracy across full-modality, bimodal, and missing-modality settings.
key_metrics.baseline: Common paradigm of directly concatenating multispectral sequences

technical_breakdown.method: A sparse Mixture-of-Experts framework that uses an explicit modality-aware routing mechanism to handle multispectral imbalance by considering both token content and spectral identity.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Sparse MoE with shared experts, interaction experts, and heterogeneous expert capacities.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Modality-aware routing that exposes spectral identity to the router; extraction of modality-unique and cross-modal synergistic information; suppression of noise-induced interference.

paper.title: Active Diffusion-Based Inference for Ill-Posed Inverse Problems under Incomplete Priors
paper.summary: Many scientific and engineering applications require estimating unknown parameters from experimentally observable data -- an inverse problem that is inherently challenging due to nonlinearity, noise, and ill-posedness. In this paper, we propose an active diffusion-based inverse problem solver. A DM is trained to learn the mapping between the parameter space and the observable space. By iteratively detecting and correcting model misspecification through posterior uncertainty, the method discovers and learns the correct region of parameter space, even when initial training bounds exclude the true parameters. This provides a principled, Bayesian justification for adaptive domain augmentation and ensures robust inference for inverse problems under incomplete prior knowledge. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our inverse solver for a toy inverse problem with infinite solutions, and for the parameterization of the quantum correlation functions to event observables in a Quantum Chromodynamics analysis of nucleon structure.
paper.comment: Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of IJCAI-ECAI 2026

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the challenge of solving ill-posed inverse problems where the true parameter values lie outside the initial prior bounds or training domain, leading to model misspecification and failed inference.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Rigidity of fixed prior distributions and domain boundaries in probabilistic generative models, which prevents robust inference when initial assumptions are incomplete or incorrect.
analysis.executive_summary: This work introduces an active learning framework for diffusion models that dynamically expands the parameter space based on posterior uncertainty, effectively correcting model misspecification. It provides a Bayesian justification for adaptive domain augmentation, enabling robust inference in scientific applications where ground truth parameters are unknown or outside initial training bounds.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Qualitative demonstration of robust inference and correct parameter discovery under incomplete priors
key_metrics.baseline: Standard diffusion-based inverse solvers with fixed prior bounds

technical_breakdown.method: An active diffusion-based solver that iteratively detects model misspecification via posterior uncertainty and corrects it by expanding the learned parameter space.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Diffusion Model (DM) trained on the mapping between parameter space and observable space, coupled with an active inference loop for domain augmentation.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Iterative detection and correction of misspecification using posterior uncertainty to guide the discovery of the correct parameter region.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Not specified in summary; likely involves iterative re-training or fine-tuning of the diffusion model as the domain expands.
